title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 32: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 1
title.raw: 卷四十二 列傳第三十二 齊高帝諸子上 Volume 42 Biographies 32: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 1

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十二齊高帝諸子上

translations.literal: Biographies 32: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 32: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part One

sentences.zh: 豫章文獻王嶷

translations.literal: Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Xiao Luan
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang

sentences.zh: 豫章文獻王嶷字宣儼，高帝第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang Xiao Luan, style name Xuanyan, was the second son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan, Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, whose style name was Xuanyan, was the second son of Emperor Gao of Qi.

sentences.zh: 寬仁弘雅，有大成之量，高帝特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: Generous, benevolent, magnanimous and refined, he possessed the capacity for great accomplishment, and Emperor Gao cherished him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and refined in bearing, with the makings of true greatness, he was especially beloved by his father Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為尚書左戶郎，錢唐令。

translations.literal: He served in Song as Left Household Minister of the Secretariat and as magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he served as Left Household Minister in the Secretariat and as magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 高帝破薛索兒，改封西陽，以先爵賜嶷，為晉壽縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao defeated Xue Suo'er, he changed his fief to Xiyang and granted Luan his former title, making him Marquis of Jinshou County.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gao defeated Xue Suo'er, he transferred his own fief to Xiyang and passed his former title to Luan, who was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinshou County.

sentences.zh: 後為武陵內史。

translations.literal: Later he became Interior Secretary of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Interior Secretary of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 時沈攸之責賧，伐荊州界內諸蠻，遂及五溪。

translations.literal: At that time Shen Youzhi imposed tribute levies and campaigned against the various barbarians within Jingzhou's borders, reaching as far as Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shen Youzhi was exacting tribute and campaigning against the various tribal peoples within Jingzhou's borders, extending his operations as far as the Five Streams region.

sentences.zh: 禁斷魚鹽，群蠻怨怒。

translations.literal: He prohibited fish and salt, and the barbarian tribes grew resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: When he banned trade in fish and salt, the tribal peoples grew resentful and angry.

sentences.zh: 酉溪蠻王田頭擬殺攸之使，攸之責賧千萬，頭擬輸五百萬，發氣死。

translations.literal: The Youxi barbarian king Tian Touni planned to kill Youzhi's envoy. Youzhi demanded ten million in tribute; Touni offered five million and died of rage.
translations.idiomatic: The Youxi barbarian king Tian Touni plotted to kill Shen Youzhi's envoy. Youzhi demanded ten million in tribute; Touni offered five million and died of apoplectic rage.

sentences.zh: 其弟婁侯篡立，頭擬子田都走入獠中。

translations.literal: His younger brother Louhou usurped the throne. Touni's son Tiandu fled among the Liao tribes.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Louhou seized power by usurpation, while Touni's son Tiandu fled into Liao territory.

sentences.zh: 於是蠻部大亂，抄掠至郡城下，嶷遣隊主張英兒擊破之。

translations.literal: The barbarian tribes then fell into great turmoil and raided up to the walls of the commandery seat. Luan sent squad leader Zhang Ying'er to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples then erupted in widespread disorder, raiding as far as the walls of the commandery seat. Luan sent squad leader Zhang Ying'er to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 田都自獠中請立，而婁侯亦歸附。

translations.literal: Tiandu asked to be installed from among the Liao, and Louhou also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandu came out of Liao territory to request installation as chief, and Louhou also submitted.

sentences.zh: 嶷誅婁侯於郡獄，命田都繼其父，蠻眾乃安。

translations.literal: Luan executed Louhou in the commandery prison, appointed Tiandu to succeed his father, and the barbarian masses were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Luan executed Louhou in the commandery prison, installed Tiandu to succeed his father, and the tribal peoples were thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 入為宋順帝驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman of the Rapid Cavalry staff under Emperor Shun of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General under Emperor Shun of Song.

sentences.zh: 詣司徒袁粲，粲謂人曰：「後來佳器也。」

translations.literal: He called on Grand Tutor Yuan Can, who said to others: "Here is an excellent vessel of later times."
translations.idiomatic: When he called on Grand Tutor Yuan Can, Can remarked to others, "Here is a vessel of excellence for the age to come."

sentences.zh: 沈攸之之難，高帝入朝堂，嶷出鎮東府，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Emperor Gao entered the imperial hall while Luan went out to guard the Eastern Palace, being promoted to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Emperor Gao entered the imperial hall while Luan went out to secure the Eastern Palace, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 及袁粲舉兵夕，丹陽丞王遜告變，先至東府，嶷遣帳內軍主戴元孫二千人隨薛道深等俱至石頭，焚門之功，元孫預焉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can raised troops that evening, Danyang Assistant Magistrate Wang Xun reported the revolt and arrived first at the Eastern Palace. Luan sent two thousand troops under his personal guard commander Dai Yuansun, who with Xue Daoshen and others reached Stone City; Dai Yuansun took part in the achievement of burning the gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening when Yuan Can raised troops in revolt, Danyang Assistant Magistrate Wang Xun reported the emergency and reached the Eastern Palace first. Luan dispatched two thousand men under his personal guard commander Dai Yuansun, who with Xue Daoshen and others advanced to Stone City; Yuansun shared in the credit for burning down the gates.

sentences.zh: 先是王蘊薦部曲六十人助為城防，實以為內應也。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Yun had recommended sixty retainers to help with city defense, but in fact intended them as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Yun had offered sixty retainers to assist in defending the city, but in fact intended them as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 嶷知蘊懷貳，不給其仗，散處外省。

translations.literal: Luan knew Yun harbored divided loyalties and did not supply them with weapons, dispersing them to posts outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, knowing that Yun harbored divided loyalties, refused to arm them and dispersed them to posts outside the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 及難作搜檢，皆已亡去。

translations.literal: When the crisis broke out and a search was conducted, they had all already fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis erupted and a search was made, they had all already fled.

sentences.zh: 上流平後，武帝自尋陽還。

translations.literal: After the upper Yangzi region was pacified, Emperor Wu returned from Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the upper Yangzi region was pacified, Emperor Wu returned from Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 嶷出為都督、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Luan went out as Area Commander and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was sent out as Area Commander and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，改封永安縣公。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling the succession, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in securing the succession, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 仍徙鎮西將軍、都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred as General Who Pacifies the West, Area Commander, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to the posts of General Who Pacifies the West, Area Commander, and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時高帝作輔，嶷務存約省，停府州儀迎物。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gao served as regent; Luan strove to practice economy and suspended the ceremonial welcome goods of the prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gao was serving as regent, Luan strove to practice economy and suspended the ceremonial welcome goods customarily furnished by the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 及至州，坦懷納善，側席思政。

translations.literal: When he reached the province, he received good counsel with an open heart and sat askew on his mat to ponder governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached his province, he received good counsel with an open heart and sat attentively to ponder matters of governance.

sentences.zh: 王儉與嶷書曰：「舊楚蕭條，仍歲多故，政荒人散，實須緝理。

translations.literal: Wang Jian wrote to Luan: "Old Chu is desolate; year after year there have been disturbances; government is neglected and the people scattered — it truly needs to be put in order."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wrote to Luan: "The old Chu region lies desolate; disturbances have followed one upon another for years, and with government neglected and the people scattered, it truly cries out for restoration."

sentences.zh: 公臨蒞甫爾，英風惟穆，江漢來蘇，八荒慕義，庾亮以來，荊州無復此政。

translations.literal: Your lordship has only just arrived, yet your noble bearing is already serene; the Jiang and Han regions are revived, and the eight directions admire your righteousness — since Yu Liang, Jingzhou has had no such governance again.
translations.idiomatic: Your lordship has only just taken up your post, yet your noble bearing is already serene; the Jiang and Han regions are reviving, and the eight directions look to your righteousness — since Yu Liang's day, Jingzhou has known nothing like this governance.

sentences.zh: 古人云'期月有成'，而公旬日成化，豈不休哉。

translations.literal: The ancients said 'in a full month there is accomplishment,' yet your lordship achieved transformation in ten days — how is this not splendid!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that in a full month one might see results, yet your lordship achieved transformation in a matter of days — what could be more splendid than this!

sentences.zh: 」初，沈攸之欲聚眾，開人相告，士庶坐執役者甚眾。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Shen Youzhi wished to gather troops, he had people inform on one another, and very many commoners and gentry were imprisoned for corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when Shen Youzhi sought to raise troops, he encouraged people to inform on one another, and a great many commoners and gentry were imprisoned for corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 嶷至鎮，一日遣三千餘人，見囚五歲刑以下不連台者，皆原遣。

translations.literal: When Luan reached his command, in a single day he released more than three thousand persons; all prisoners under five years' sentence not connected with the central government were pardoned and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan reached his post, in a single day he released more than three thousand persons; all prisoners serving sentences of five years or less who were not implicated in central-government cases were pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 以市稅重，多所寬假。

translations.literal: Because market taxes were heavy, he granted many exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: Because market taxes had grown burdensome, he granted many exemptions.

sentences.zh: 百姓甚悅。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 禪讓之間，武帝欲速定大業，嶷依違其事，默無所言。

translations.literal: During the abdication proceedings, Emperor Wu wished to settle the great enterprise quickly; Luan wavered on the matter and said nothing in silence.
translations.idiomatic: During the abdication proceedings, Emperor Wu wished to settle the succession quickly; Luan hesitated on the matter and remained silent.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，高帝即位，赦詔未至，嶷先下令蠲除部內升明二年以前逋負。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Emperor Gao took the throne; before the amnesty edict arrived, Luan first ordered the cancellation of all arrears within his jurisdiction dating before the second year of Shengming.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan, when Emperor Gao took the throne, Luan issued orders to cancel all arrears within his jurisdiction dating before the second year of Shengming, even before the amnesty edict arrived from the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書令、都督、揚州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封豫章郡王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Area Commander, Inspector of Yangzhou, Grand General of the Rapid Cavalry, and Bearer of the Grand Staff with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Area Commander, Inspector of Yangzhou, Grand General of the Rapid Cavalry, and Bearer of the Grand Staff with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 會魏軍動，詔以嶷為南蠻校尉、荊湘二州刺史，都督八州。

translations.literal: When Wei troops stirred, an edict appointed Luan Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, Inspector of the two provinces Jing and Xiang, and Area Commander over eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces stirred on the frontier, an edict appointed Luan Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, Inspector of Jing and Xiang, and Area Commander over eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋給油絡俠望車。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was granted an oil-lacquered carriage with an escort canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was granted an oil-lacquered carriage with an escort canopy.

sentences.zh: 二年，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: In the second year he was granted twenty halberd-bearing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was granted twenty halberd-bearing attendants.

sentences.zh: 其夏，于南蠻園東南開館立學，上表言狀。

translations.literal: That summer, southeast of the Southern Barbarians Garden he opened a hall and established a school, submitting a memorial describing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, southeast of the Southern Barbarians Garden, he opened a hall and established a school, submitting a memorial describing his plan.

sentences.zh: 置生三十人，取舊族父祖位正佐台郎年二十五以下十五以上補之。

translations.literal: He enrolled thirty students, selecting men of old families whose fathers and grandfathers had held regular assistant posts as secretariat gentlemen, between fifteen and twenty-five years of age, to fill the places.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled thirty students, drawn from old families whose fathers and grandfathers had held regular assistant posts as secretariat gentlemen, between the ages of fifteen and twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 置儒林參軍一人，文學祭酒一人，勸學從事二人。

translations.literal: He appointed one Confucian Forest Adjutant, one Libationer of Letters, and two Assistants for Encouraging Study.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed one Confucian Forest Adjutant, one Libationer of Letters, and two Assistants for Encouraging Study.

sentences.zh: 行釋菜禮。

translations.literal: He performed the ceremony of offering vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: He performed the ceremonial offering of vegetables to inaugurate the school.

sentences.zh: 以穀過賤，聽人以米當口錢，優評斛一百。

translations.literal: Because grain was excessively cheap, he permitted people to pay head taxes in rice at a favorable rate of one hundred measures per assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain had become excessively cheap, he permitted people to pay head taxes in rice at a favorable rate of one hundred measures per assessment.

sentences.zh: 義陽劫帥張群亡命積年，鼓行為賊，義陽、武陵、天門、南平四郡界被其殘破，沈攸之連討不禽，末乃首用之。

translations.literal: Yiyang bandit chief Zhang Qun had been a fugitive for many years, marching in formation as a robber; the borders of the four commanderies Yiyang, Wuling, Tianmen, and Nanping were ravaged by him. Shen Youzhi campaigned against him repeatedly without capturing him, and in the end employed him by accepting his submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Yiyang bandit chief Zhang Qun had been an outlaw for many years, marching his followers in formation as raiders; the borders of Yiyang, Wuling, Tianmen, and Nanping were ravaged by him. Shen Youzhi campaigned against him repeatedly without success, and in the end took him into service by accepting his submission.

sentences.zh: 攸之起事，群從下郢，于路先叛，結柴於三溪，依據深險。

translations.literal: When Youzhi raised troops, Qun followed him down to Ying; on the road he rebelled first, building stockades at Sanxi and relying on deep and perilous terrain.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi raised troops in rebellion, Qun followed him toward Ying; on the march he rebelled first, building stockades at Sanxi and holding ground in deep and perilous terrain.

sentences.zh: 嶷遣中兵參軍虞欣祖為義陽太守，使降意誘納之，厚為禮遺，於坐斬首，其黨皆散，四郡獲安。

translations.literal: Luan sent Central Troops Adjutant Yu Xingu as Administrator of Yiyang to win him over with conciliatory intent; treating him with generous gifts, he beheaded him at the banquet, his followers all scattered, and the four commanderies were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Luan sent Central Troops Adjutant Yu Xingu as Administrator of Yiyang to win Qun over with conciliatory gestures; treating him with generous gifts, he beheaded him at the banquet table. Qun's followers scattered, and the four commanderies were secured.

sentences.zh: 入為中書監、司空、揚州刺史，都督二州，侍中如故，加兵置佐，以前軍臨川王映府文武配司空。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Yangzhou, Area Commander over two provinces, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before, with added military staff; the civil and military officials of the former army Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying's establishment were assigned to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Yangzhou, Area Commander over two provinces, retaining his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary with added military staff; the civil and military officials of the former army Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying's establishment were assigned to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 嶷以將還都，修廨宇及路陌，東歸部曲不得齎府州物出城。

translations.literal: As Luan was about to return to the capital, he repaired official buildings and roads; his eastern-returning retainers were not permitted to carry prefectural or provincial goods out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: As Luan prepared to return to the capital, he repaired official buildings and roads, and forbade his retainers returning east to carry prefectural or provincial goods out of the city.

sentences.zh: 發江津，士女觀送數千人皆垂泣。

translations.literal: Setting out from Jiangjin, several thousand men and women who came to see him off all wept.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out from Jiangjin, several thousand men and women who came to see him off wept as they watched him depart.

sentences.zh: 嶷發江陵感疾，至都未瘳，上深憂慮，為之大赦，三年六月壬子赦令是也。

translations.literal: Luan fell ill after leaving Jiangling; he had not recovered when he reached the capital. The emperor was deeply anxious and proclaimed a great amnesty on his account — this was the amnesty edict of the renzi day in the sixth month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Luan fell ill after leaving Jiangling and had not recovered by the time he reached the capital. The emperor was deeply anxious and proclaimed a great amnesty on his account — this was the amnesty edict of the renzi day in the sixth month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，上幸東府，設金石樂，使乘輿至宮六門。

translations.literal: When his illness abated, the emperor visited the Eastern Palace, set out bronze and stone music, and had the imperial carriage proceed to the six gates of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered, the emperor visited the Eastern Palace, arranged bronze and stone music, and had the imperial carriage proceed as far as the six gates of the palace.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，進位太尉，增置兵佐，解侍中，增班劍三十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Luan was promoted to Grand Commandant, with additional military staff; he relinquished Attendant-in-Ordinary and was granted thirty halberd-bearing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Luan was promoted to Grand Commandant with additional military staff; he relinquished his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary and was granted thirty halberd-bearing attendants.

sentences.zh: 建元中，武帝以事失旨，高帝頗有代嫡之意。

translations.literal: During the Jianyuan era, Emperor Wu lost favor over some matter, and Emperor Gao quite had the intention of replacing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyuan era, Emperor Wu lost favor over some matter, and Emperor Gao came to favor replacing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 而嶷事武帝恭悌盡禮，未嘗違忤顏色，故武帝友愛亦深。

translations.literal: But Luan served Emperor Wu with full courtesy and respectful deference, never once offending his expression, and so Emperor Wu's affection for him was also deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Luan served Emperor Wu with full courtesy and respectful deference, never once giving offense, and so the emperor's affection for him remained deep as well.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，高帝崩，哭泣過度，眼耳皆出血。

translations.literal: By nature he was supremely filial; when Emperor Gao died, he wept excessively and blood issued from his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial; when Emperor Gao died, he wept so excessively that blood issued from his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，領太子太傅，解中書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he served as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and relinquished the Directorship of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and relinquished the Directorship of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宋武以來，州郡秩俸及雜供給，多隨土所出，無有定準。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wu of Song, provincial and commandery salaries and miscellaneous supplies have largely followed what each region produces, with no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wu of Song's day, provincial and commandery salaries and miscellaneous supplies had largely followed whatever each region produced, with no fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 嶷上表請明立定格，班下四方，永為恒制，從之。

translations.literal: Luan submitted a memorial requesting that fixed standards be clearly established and promulgated to the four directions as a permanent regulation; his request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Luan submitted a memorial requesting that fixed standards be clearly established and promulgated throughout the realm as a permanent regulation; his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 嶷不參朝務，而言事密謀，多見信納。

translations.literal: Luan did not participate in court affairs, yet in confidential counsel his words were often trusted and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Luan did not participate in routine court affairs, yet in confidential counsel his words were often trusted and adopted.

sentences.zh: 服闋，加侍中。

translations.literal: When his mourning period ended, he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was given the additional post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉制，諸王入齋合，得白服裙帽見人主，唯出太極四廂，乃備朝衣。

translations.literal: Under the Yuanjia regulations of Song, when princes entered the fasting quarters they might wear white garments with skirt and cap to see the sovereign; only when leaving the four wings of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate did they don court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuanjia regulations of Song, when princes entered the fasting quarters they might wear white garments with skirt and cap to see the sovereign; only when leaving the four wings of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate did they don full court dress.

sentences.zh: 自比以來，此事一斷。

translations.literal: Since then this practice has been entirely discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: Since then this practice had been entirely discontinued.

sentences.zh: 上與嶷同生相友睦，宮內曲宴，許依元嘉。

translations.literal: The emperor and Luan were born of the same mother and were friendly and close; at private palace banquets he was permitted to follow the Yuanjia practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Luan shared the same mother and were close friends; at private palace banquets the emperor permitted him to follow the Yuanjia practice.

sentences.zh: 嶷固辭，不奉敕；

translations.literal: Luan firmly declined and did not obey the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Luan firmly declined and did not obey the edict;

sentences.zh: 唯車駕幸第，乃白服烏紗帽以侍宴焉。

translations.literal: only when the imperial carriage visited his residence did he wear white garments and a black gauze cap to attend the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: only when the imperial carriage visited his residence did he wear white garments and a black gauze cap to attend the banquet.

sentences.zh: 至於衣服制度，動皆陳啟，事無專制，務從減省，並不見許。

translations.literal: As for clothing regulations, he invariably submitted memorials on every matter, never acting on his own authority, always striving for reduction — and none of it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: As for regulations governing dress and furnishings, he invariably submitted memorials on every matter, never acting on his own authority and always striving for reduction — and none of it was approved.

sentences.zh: 又啟曰：「北第舊邸，本自甚華，臣往歲作小眠齋，皆補接為辦，無乖格制。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying: "The old residence of the Northern Mansion was originally very splendid; last year I built a small sleeping hall, all patched and fitted out in compliance, without violating regulations."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial saying, "The old residence of the Northern Mansion was originally quite splendid; last year I built a small sleeping hall, all patched and fitted out in compliance, without violating regulations."

sentences.zh: 要是檉柏之華，一時新淨，東府又有此齋，亦為華屋，而臣頓有二處住止，下情竊所未安。

translations.literal: "Yet it was merely the splendor of tamarisk and cypress, fresh and new for a time; the Eastern Palace also has such a hall, likewise a splendid dwelling, and I suddenly have two places of residence — in my humble feeling I am privately ill at ease."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet it was merely the splendor of tamarisk and cypress, fresh and new for a time; the Eastern Palace also has such a hall, likewise a splendid dwelling, and I suddenly find myself with two places of residence — in my humble feeling I am privately ill at ease."

sentences.zh: 訊訪東宮玄圃，乃有柏屋，制甚古拙，臣乃欲壞取以奉太子，非但失之於前，且補接既多，不可見移，亦恐外物或為異論，不審可有垂許送東府齋理不？

translations.literal: "Inquiring at the Eastern Palace's Dark Garden, there is a cypress hall, very antiquated in design; I wish to dismantle it and offer it to the Heir Apparent — not only would this be a loss to what went before, but with so many patchings it cannot be moved intact, and I fear outsiders might raise objections. Might I be permitted to send the Eastern Palace hall for repair instead?"
translations.idiomatic: "Inquiring at the Eastern Palace's Dark Garden, I found a cypress hall, very antiquated in design; I wished to dismantle it and offer it to the Heir Apparent — not only would this be a loss to what went before, but with so many patchings it cannot be moved intact, and I fear outsiders might raise objections. Might I be permitted to send the Eastern Palace hall for repair instead?"

sentences.zh: 」上答曰：「見別紙，汝勞疾，亦復那得不動，何意為作煩長啟事。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied: "I have seen your separate note. You are worn by illness — how could you not be stirred? Why make such a tedious, lengthy memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "I have seen your separate note. You are worn by illness — how could you not be stirred? Why submit such a tedious, lengthy memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不從。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he did not consent.

sentences.zh: 三年，文惠太子講孝經畢，嶷求解太傅，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Crown Prince Wenhu finished lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety, Luan requested to be relieved of the Grand Tutorship; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Crown Prince Wenhu finished lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety, Luan requested to be relieved of the Grand Tutorship; his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 嶷常慮盛滿，又因言宴求解揚州授竟陵王子良，上終不許，曰：「畢汝一世，無所多言。」

translations.literal: Luan often feared reaching the fullness of eminence; on another occasion at a banquet he requested to relinquish Yangzhou and grant it to Ziliang, Prince of Jingling. The emperor ultimately refused, saying: "Finish out your lifetime — say no more about it."
translations.idiomatic: Luan often feared the perils of eminence at its height; on another occasion at a banquet he requested to relinquish Yangzhou and grant it to Ziliang, Prince of Jingling. The emperor ultimately refused, saying, "Finish out your lifetime in these posts — say no more about it."

sentences.zh: 武帝即位後，頻發詔拜陵，不果行，遣嶷拜陵。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu took the throne, edicts to visit the imperial tombs were issued repeatedly but he could not go; he sent Luan to perform the tomb visit.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne, edicts to visit the imperial tombs were issued repeatedly, but he could not go himself and sent Luan to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 還過延陵季子廟，觀沸井，有水牛突部伍，直兵執牛推問，嶷不許，取絹一疋，橫系牛角，放歸其家。

translations.literal: On his return he passed the temple of Master Ji of Yanling and viewed the boiling well; a water buffalo charged into his retinue, and the guards seized the buffalo for interrogation. Luan forbade this, took a bolt of silk, tied it crosswise to the buffalo's horns, and sent it home.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed the temple of Master Ji of Yanling and viewed the boiling well; when a water buffalo charged into his retinue, the guards seized it for interrogation. Luan forbade this, took a bolt of silk, tied it crosswise to the animal's horns, and sent it home.

sentences.zh: 政在寬厚，故得朝野歡心。

translations.literal: His governance lay in generosity and leniency, and so he won the hearts of court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: His governance lay in generosity and leniency, and so he won the hearts of court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 四年，唐宇之賊起，嶷啟上曰：「此段小寇，出於凶愚，天網宏罩，理不足論。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the bandits of Tang Yuzhi rose. Luan submitted to the emperor: "This petty band of robbers springs from vicious folly; the heavenly net is vast in its cover — they are hardly worth discussing."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the bandits led by Tang Yuzhi rose in revolt. Luan submitted to the emperor, "This petty band springs from vicious folly; the heavenly net is vast in its cover — they are hardly worth discussing."

sentences.zh: 但聖明禦世，幸可不爾。

translations.literal: "Yet under sagely illumination governing the age, one may hope it need not be so."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet under your sagely rule, one may hope matters need not come to this."

sentences.zh: 比藉聲聽，皆云有由而然。

translations.literal: "According to what one hears by rumor, all say there are reasons why it has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: "According to what one hears, all say there are reasons why it has come to this."

sentences.zh: 但頃小大士庶，每以小利奉公，不顧所損者大。

translations.literal: "Yet recently minor officials and commoners, for small profit in serving the public, disregard how great the damage may be."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet recently minor officials and commoners alike, chasing small profit in serving the public interest, disregard how great the damage may be."

sentences.zh: 擿籍檢功巧，督恤簡小塘，藏丁匿口，凡諸條制，實長怨府。

translations.literal: "Scrutinizing household registers, inspecting crafty labor contributions, supervising relief for small ponds, concealing corvée laborers and hidden households — all such regulations truly breed a treasury of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: "Scrutinizing household registers, inspecting crafty labor contributions, supervising relief works on small ponds, concealing corvée laborers and unregistered households — all such regulations truly breed a treasury of resentment."

sentences.zh: 此目前交利，非天下大計。

translations.literal: "This is immediate mutual profit, not the great plan for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: "This serves immediate mutual profit, not the great plan for the realm."

sentences.zh: 一室之中，尚不可精，宇宙之內，何可周洗。

translations.literal: "Within a single room one still cannot be thorough; within the whole cosmos, how can one wash everything clean?"
translations.idiomatic: "Within a single room one still cannot be thorough; within the whole cosmos, how can one wash everything clean?"

sentences.zh: 公家何嘗不知人多欺巧，古今政以不可細碎，故不為耳。

translations.literal: "The government has never not known that many people practice deceit and craft — from antiquity to the present, policy has simply held that one cannot be minutely exhaustive, and so does not act."
translations.idiomatic: "The government has never been unaware that many people practice deceit and craft — from antiquity to the present, policy has simply held that one cannot be minutely exhaustive, and so does not act."

sentences.zh: 為此者實非乖理，但識理者百不有一。

translations.literal: "To act in this way is in truth not contrary to reason, but those who understand reason are not one in a hundred."
translations.idiomatic: "To act in this way is in truth not contrary to reason, but those who understand reason are not one in a hundred."

sentences.zh: 陛下弟兒大臣，猶不能伏理，況復天下，悠悠萬品？

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's younger brothers and great ministers still cannot submit to reason — how much less the myriad classes throughout the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's younger brothers and great ministers still cannot submit to reason — how much less the myriad classes throughout the realm?"

sentences.zh: 怨積聚黨，凶迷相類，止于一處，何足不除，脫復多所，便成紜紜。

translations.literal: "Resentment accumulates and factions form; the vicious and deluded resemble one another. Confined to one place, how could they not be eliminated? But if they arise in many places, disorder will ensue."
translations.idiomatic: "Resentment accumulates and factions form; the vicious and deluded resemble one another. Confined to one place, how could they not be eliminated? But if they arise in many places, disorder will ensue."

sentences.zh: 」上答曰：「欺巧那可容！

translations.literal: " The emperor replied: "How can deceit and craft be tolerated!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "How can deceit and craft be tolerated!"

sentences.zh: 宋世混亂，以為是不？

translations.literal: "Was the chaos of the Song age not thought sufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: "Was the chaos of the Song age not thought sufficient warning?"

sentences.zh: 蚊蟻何足為憂，至今都應散滅。

translations.literal: "Mosquitoes and ants are hardly worth worrying over — by now they should all have scattered and perished."
translations.idiomatic: "Mosquitoes and ants are hardly worth worrying over — by now they should all have scattered and perished."

sentences.zh: 吾政恨其不辦大耳，亦何時無亡命邪。

translations.literal: "My regret is only that they did not make something bigger of it — when has there ever been a time without fugitives?"
translations.idiomatic: "My only regret is that they did not make something bigger of it — when has there ever been a time without outlaws?"

sentences.zh: 」後乃詔聽復籍注。

translations.literal: " Later an edict permitted the restoration of household registration.
translations.idiomatic: " Later an edict permitted the restoration of household registration.

sentences.zh: 是時武帝奢侈，後宮萬餘人，宮內不容，太樂、景第、暴室皆滿，猶以為未足。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wu was extravagant; his rear palace had more than ten thousand persons, and the palace could not contain them — the Grand Music Office, the Scenic Residence, and the Detention Chambers were all full, yet he still thought it insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Emperor Wu was extravagant; his rear palace held more than ten thousand persons, and the palace could not contain them — the Grand Music Office, the Scenic Residence, and the Detention Chambers were all full, yet he still thought it insufficient.

sentences.zh: 嶷後房亦千餘人。

translations.literal: Luan's rear chambers also had more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's own rear chambers also held more than a thousand women.

sentences.zh: 潁川荀丕獻書於嶷，極言其失，嶷咨嗟良久，為書答之，又為之減遣。

translations.literal: Xun Pi of Yingchuan submitted a letter to Luan, speaking to the utmost of his faults; Luan sighed long and wrote a reply, and also reduced his retinue on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Pi of Yingchuan submitted a letter to Luan, speaking bluntly of his faults; Luan sighed at length, wrote a reply, and also reduced his household on account of it.

sentences.zh: 丕字令哲，後為荊州西曹書佐，長史王秀與其書，題之云：「西曹荀君」。

translations.literal: Pi, style name Lingzhe, later became Western Bureau Secretary of Jingzhou; Chief Clerk Wang Xiu wrote to him, addressing the letter "Lord Xun of the Western Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Pi, whose style name was Lingzhe, later became Western Bureau Secretary of Jingzhou; Chief Clerk Wang Xiu wrote to him, addressing the letter "Lord Xun of the Western Bureau."

sentences.zh: 丕報書曰：「第五之位，不減驃騎，亦不知西曹何殊長史！

translations.literal: Pi replied: "The fifth-rank post is no less than Rapid Cavalry General — and how is the Western Bureau different from Chief Clerk!"
translations.idiomatic: Pi replied, "The fifth-rank post is no less than Rapid Cavalry General — and how is the Western Bureau different from Chief Clerk!"

sentences.zh: 且人之處世，當以德行稱著，何遽以一爵高人邪？

translations.literal: "Moreover, in one's conduct in the world one should be known for virtue and conduct — why hasten to elevate a man by a mere rank?"
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, in one's conduct in the world one should be known for virtue and character — why hasten to elevate a man by a mere rank?"

sentences.zh: 相如不見屈于澠池，毛遂安受辱於郢都，造敵臨事，僕必先於二子，未知足下之貴，足下之威，孰若秦、楚兩王。

translations.literal: Lin Xiangru was not seen to yield at Mianchi, yet Mao Sui calmly accepted humiliation at Ying — when facing the enemy in the moment of crisis, your servant would surely go before these two. I do not know your lordship's eminence or your lordship's authority — how do they compare with the kings of Qin and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiangru was not seen to yield at Mianchi, yet Mao Sui calmly accepted humiliation at Ying — when facing the enemy in the moment of crisis, I would surely go before these two. I do not know your eminence or your authority — how do they compare with the kings of Qin and Chu?

sentences.zh: 僕以德為寶，足下以位為寶，各寶其寶，於此敬宜。

translations.literal: Your servant takes virtue as his treasure; your lordship takes rank as his treasure — each treasures his own treasure, and in this respect deference is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I take virtue as my treasure; you take rank as yours — each treasures his own treasure, and in this respect deference is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」於是直題云：「長史王君」。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he addressed it directly: "Chief Clerk Lord Wang."
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he addressed it directly: "Chief Clerk Lord Wang."

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王儉當朝，丕又與儉書曰：「足下建高人之名，而不顯高人之跡，將何以書于齊史哉。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian held the court; Pi also wrote to Jian: "Your lordship has built the name of a lofty man, yet does not display the conduct of a lofty man — how will this be written in the history of Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian held the court; Pi also wrote to Jian: "You have built the name of a lofty man, yet do not display the conduct of a lofty man — how will this be written in the history of Qi?"

sentences.zh: 」及南郡綱紀啟荊州刺史隨王子隆請罪丕，丕自申乃免。

translations.literal: " When the chief steward of Nan Commandery reported to Jingzhou Inspector Sui, Prince Zilong, requesting that Pi be punished, Pi defended himself and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " When the chief steward of Nan Commandery reported to Jingzhou Inspector Sui, Prince Zilong, requesting that Pi be punished, Pi defended himself and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 又上書極諫武帝，言甚直，帝不悅，丕竟於荊州獄賜死。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial remonstrating Emperor Wu to the utmost; his words were very blunt and the emperor was displeased. Pi was ultimately ordered to die by suicide in the Jingzhou prison.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a memorial remonstrating Emperor Wu to the utmost; his words were very blunt and the emperor was displeased. Pi was ultimately ordered to die by suicide in the Jingzhou prison.

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣聞其死，曰：「丕縱有罪，亦不應殺，數千年後，其如竹帛何！」

translations.literal: When Xu Xiaosi heard of his death, he said: "Even if Pi had guilt, he should not have been killed — thousands of years hence, what will become of his name on bamboo and silk!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Xiaosi heard of his death, he said, "Even if Pi had guilt, he should not have been killed — thousands of years hence, what will become of his name in the historical record!"

sentences.zh: 五年，嶷進位大司馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Luan was promoted to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Luan was promoted to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 八年，給皁輪車。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was granted a black-wheeled carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was granted a black-wheeled carriage.

sentences.zh: 尋加中書監，固讓。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was given the additional post of Director of the Secretariat, which he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was offered the additional post of Director of the Secretariat, which he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 嶷身長七尺八寸，善持容范，文物衛從，禮冠百僚。

translations.literal: Luan stood seven feet eight inches in height, skilled in maintaining dignified bearing; his ceremonial regalia and attendants outshone all the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Luan stood seven feet eight inches in height and was skilled in maintaining dignified bearing; his ceremonial regalia and attendants outshone all the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 每出入殿省，皆瞻望嚴肅。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered or left the palace halls, all gazed upon him with solemn respect.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered or left the palace halls, all gazed upon him with solemn respect.

sentences.zh: 自以地位隆重，深懷退素，北宅舊有園田之美，乃盛修理之。

translations.literal: Considering his position weighty and eminent, he deeply cherished simplicity and retirement; the Northern Mansion's old gardens and fields were beautiful, and he undertook extensive repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Considering his position weighty and eminent, he deeply cherished simplicity and retirement; the Northern Mansion's old gardens and fields were beautiful, and he undertook extensive repairs.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問臨川王映居家何事樂，映曰：「政使劉瓛講禮，顧則講易，朱廣之講莊、老，臣與二三諸彥兄弟友生時復擊贊，以此為樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying what he found pleasurable at home. Ying replied: "I have Liu Huan lecture on ritual, Gu Ze on the Changes, Zhu Guangzhi on Zhuangzi and Laozi; I with two or three worthy brothers and student friends occasionally strike the clappers — this is my pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying what he found pleasurable at home. Ying replied, "I have Liu Huan lecture on ritual, Gu Ze on the Changes, Zhu Guangzhi on Zhuangzi and Laozi; I with two or three worthy brothers and student friends occasionally strike the clappers — this is my pleasure."

sentences.zh: 」上大賞之。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor greatly praised this.

sentences.zh: 他日謂嶷曰：「臨川為善，遂至於斯。

translations.literal: Another day he said to Luan: "Linchuan does good — and has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Another day he said to Luan, "Linchuan does good — and has come to this."

sentences.zh: 」嶷曰：「此大司馬公之次弟，安得不爾！

translations.literal: " Luan said: "This is the Grand Marshal's younger brother — how could he not be so!"
translations.idiomatic: " Luan said, "This is the Grand Marshal's younger brother — how could he not be so!"

sentences.zh: 」上仍以玉如意指嶷曰：「未若皇帝之次弟為善最多也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor still pointed at Luan with his jade ruyi scepter and said: "Not so good as the emperor's younger brother, who does the most good of all."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still pointed at Luan with his jade ruyi scepter and said, "Not so good as the emperor's younger brother, who does the most good of all."

sentences.zh: 嶷常戒諸子曰：「凡富貴少不驕奢，以約失之者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Luan often admonished his sons: "Among the wealthy and noble, few are not arrogant and extravagant — those who fail through restraint are rare."
translations.idiomatic: Luan often admonished his sons, "Among the wealthy and noble, few are not arrogant and extravagant — those who fail through restraint are rare."

sentences.zh: 漢世以來，侯王子弟，以驕恣之故，大者滅身喪族，小者削奪邑地，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: "Since the Han dynasty, marquises and princes' sons and younger brothers, through arrogant willfulness, have in great cases lost their lives and clans, in small cases been stripped of fiefs and lands — can one not take warning!"
translations.idiomatic: "Since the Han dynasty, marquises and princes' sons and younger brothers, through arrogant willfulness, have in great cases lost their lives and clans, in small cases been stripped of fiefs and lands — can one not take warning!"

sentences.zh: 」稱疾不利住東城，累求還第，令世子子廉代鎮東府。

translations.literal: " He pleaded illness and found it disadvantageous to dwell in the Eastern City; repeatedly he requested to return to his mansion and had his heir Zilian replace him in guarding the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He pleaded illness and found it disadvantageous to dwell in the Eastern City; repeatedly he requested to return to his mansion and had his heir Zilian replace him in guarding the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上數幸嶷第，宋長寧陵隧道出第前路，上曰：「我便是入他家墓內尋人。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited Luan's mansion; the tunnel of Song's Changning Mausoleum emerged onto the road before the mansion. The emperor said: "I am simply entering someone else's tomb to find a man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Luan's mansion; the tunnel of Song's Changning Mausoleum emerged onto the road before the mansion. The emperor said, "I am simply entering someone else's tomb to find a man."

sentences.zh: 」乃徙其表闕騏驎於東岡。

translations.literal: " He then moved the ornamental gate towers and qilin statues to the eastern hill.
translations.idiomatic: " He then moved the ornamental gate towers and qilin statues to the eastern hill.

sentences.zh: 騏驎及闕，形勢甚巧，宋孝武於襄陽致之，後諸帝王陵皆模範，而莫及也。

translations.literal: The qilin and gate towers were very artful in form; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had them brought from Xiangyang; later all imperial tombs took them as models, yet none could match them.
translations.idiomatic: The qilin and gate towers were very artful in form; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had them brought from Xiangyang; later all imperial tombs took them as models, yet none could match them.

sentences.zh: 永明末，車駕數遊幸，唯嶷陪從。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongming era, the imperial carriage made many excursions and tours; only Luan accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongming era, the imperial carriage made many excursions and tours; only Luan accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗出新林苑，同輦夜歸，至宮門，嶷下輦辭出，上曰：「今夜行，無使為尉司所呵也。

translations.literal: The emperor once went out to Xinlin Park and returned at night in the same carriage; at the palace gate Luan descended from the carriage to take his leave. The emperor said: "Traveling tonight — don't let the patrol officers rebuke you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once went out to Xinlin Park and returned at night in the same carriage; at the palace gate Luan descended to take his leave. The emperor said, "Traveling tonight — don't let the patrol officers rebuke you."

sentences.zh: 」嶷對曰：「京輦之內，皆屬臣州，願陛下不垂過慮。」

translations.literal: " Luan replied: "Within the capital precinct all falls under my province — may Your Majesty not trouble yourself with excessive concern."
translations.idiomatic: " Luan replied, "Within the capital precinct all falls under my province — may Your Majesty not trouble yourself with excessive concern."

sentences.zh: 上大笑，賜以魏所送氈車。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and granted him the felt carriage sent by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed greatly and granted him the felt carriage sent by Wei.

sentences.zh: 每幸第，不復屏人，敕外監曰：「我往大司馬第，是還家耳。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited the mansion he no longer screened out attendants, instructing the outer supervisor: "When I go to the Grand Marshal's mansion, I am simply returning home."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he visited the mansion he no longer screened out attendants, instructing the outer supervisor, "When I go to the Grand Marshal's mansion, I am simply returning home."

sentences.zh: 」嶷妃庾氏，嘗有疾，瘳，上幸嶷邸，後堂設金石樂，宮人畢至。

translations.literal: " Luan's consort, the Lady Yu, had once been ill and recovered; the emperor visited Luan's residence, bronze and stone music was set up in the rear hall, and palace women all attended.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan's consort, the Lady Yu, had once been ill and recovered; the emperor visited Luan's residence, bronze and stone music was set up in the rear hall, and palace women all attended.

sentences.zh: 登桐台，使嶷著烏紗帽，極日盡歡，敕嶷備家人之禮。

translations.literal: They ascended the Tong Terrace; the emperor had Luan wear a black gauze cap and enjoy the day to the fullest, ordering Luan to prepare family ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the Tong Terrace; the emperor had Luan wear a black gauze cap and enjoy the day to the fullest, ordering Luan to prepare family ceremony.

sentences.zh: 嶷謂上曰：「古來言願陛下壽比南山，或稱萬歲，此殆近貌言。

translations.literal: Luan said to the emperor: "Since antiquity people have said they wish Your Majesty's life equal to the Southern Mountain, or called out 'ten thousand years' — this is nearly superficial speech."
translations.idiomatic: Luan said to the emperor, "Since antiquity people have said they wish Your Majesty's life equal to the Southern Mountain, or called out 'ten thousand years' — this is nearly superficial speech."

sentences.zh: 如臣所懷，實願陛下極壽百年亦足矣。

translations.literal: "As in this servant's heart, I truly wish Your Majesty the utmost span of a hundred years — that would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: "As in my heart, I truly wish Your Majesty the utmost span of a hundred years — that would be enough."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「百年復何可得，止得東西一百，於事亦濟。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "A hundred years — how could that be attained? Only east and west a hundred — that would also suffice for the matter."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "A hundred years — how could that be attained? Only east and west a hundred — that would also suffice for the matter."

sentences.zh: 」因相執流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they grasped each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they grasped each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 十年，上封嶷諸子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor enfeoffed Luan's sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the emperor enfeoffed Luan's sons.

sentences.zh: 舊例王子封千戶，嶷欲五子俱封，啟減，人五百戶。

translations.literal: By old precedent princes' sons were enfeoffed with a thousand households; Luan wished all five sons to be enfeoffed and submitted a request to reduce each to five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: By old precedent princes' sons were enfeoffed with a thousand households; Luan wished all five sons to be enfeoffed and submitted a request to reduce each to five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年疾篤，表解職，不許，賜錢五百萬營功德。

translations.literal: That year his illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial requesting to resign his posts, which was not granted; he was granted five million in cash to perform meritorious works.
translations.idiomatic: That year his illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial requesting to resign his posts, which was not granted; he was granted five million in cash to perform meritorious works.

sentences.zh: 薨，年四十九。

translations.literal: He died; he was forty-nine years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其日上視疾，至薨乃還宮。

translations.literal: That day the emperor visited him in his illness and did not return to the palace until his death.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor visited him in his illness and did not return to the palace until his death.

sentences.zh: 詔斂以袞冕之服，溫明秘器，大鴻臚持節護喪事，太官朝夕送祭奠，大司馬、太傅二府文武悉停過葬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him dressed in imperial robes and crown, with the Warm Bright secret coffin; the Grand Herald held the staff to oversee funeral affairs; the Imperial Kitchen sent offerings morning and evening; all civil and military officials of the Grand Marshal and Grand Tutor establishments suspended work past the burial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him dressed in imperial robes and crown, with the Warm Bright secret coffin; the Grand Herald held the staff to oversee funeral affairs; the Imperial Kitchen sent offerings morning and evening; all civil and military officials of the Grand Marshal and Grand Tutor establishments suspended work past the burial.

sentences.zh: 詔贈假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、揚州牧，綠綟綬，具九服錫命之禮，侍中、大司馬、太傅、王如故。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Area Commander over all armies within and without, Chancellor, and Governor of Yangzhou, with green ribbon and tassel, fully performing the nine-garment investiture ceremony; Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor, and Prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Area Commander over all armies within and without, Chancellor, and Governor of Yangzhou, with green ribbon and tassel, fully performing the nine-garment investiture ceremony; his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor, and Prince were confirmed as before.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鸞輅，黃屋左纛，虎賁班劍百人，轀輬車，前後部羽葆、鼓吹。

translations.literal: He was granted the nine-tassel imperial carriage with phoenix canopy, yellow roof and left banner, a hundred Tiger Guard halberd-bearers, the encoffining carriage, and front and rear escorts with feather parasols and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the nine-tassel imperial carriage with phoenix canopy, yellow roof and left banner, a hundred Tiger Guard halberd-bearers, the encoffining carriage, and front and rear escorts with feather parasols and martial music.

sentences.zh: 喪葬送儀，並依漢東平王蒼故事。

translations.literal: Funeral and burial rites all followed the precedent of Han's Prince of Dongping, Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral and burial rites all followed the precedent of Han's Prince of Dongping, Cang.

sentences.zh: 嶷臨終，召子子廉、子恪曰：「吾無後，當共相勉勵，篤睦為先。

translations.literal: At his end Luan summoned his sons Zilian and Zike and said: "I have no further days — you should encourage one another, taking sincere harmony as foremost."
translations.idiomatic: At his end Luan summoned his sons Zilian and Zike and said, "I have no further days — you should encourage one another, taking sincere harmony as foremost."

sentences.zh: 才有優劣，位有通塞，運有富貧，此自然理，無足以相陵侮。

translations.literal: "Talent has superior and inferior; position has smooth and blocked; fortune has rich and poor — this is natural principle, insufficient grounds for mutual bullying."
translations.idiomatic: "Talent has superior and inferior; position has smooth and blocked; fortune has rich and poor — this is natural principle, insufficient grounds for mutual bullying."

sentences.zh: 勤學行，守基業，修閨庭，尚閑素，如此足無憂患。

translations.literal: "Study diligently and practice conduct, guard the family estate, keep the inner household in order, esteem simplicity — thus one may be free of worry."
translations.idiomatic: "Study diligently and practice conduct, guard the family estate, keep the inner household in order, esteem simplicity — thus one may be free of worry."

sentences.zh: 聖主儲皇及諸親賢，亦當不以吾沒易情也。

translations.literal: "The sage sovereign, the Heir Apparent, and all kinsmen and worthies likewise should not change their feelings because of my passing."
translations.idiomatic: "The sage sovereign, the Heir Apparent, and all kinsmen and worthies likewise should not change their feelings because of my passing."

sentences.zh: 三日施靈，惟香火、盤水、乾飯、酒脯、檳榔而已，朔望菜食一盤，加以甘果，此外悉省。

translations.literal: "For the three-day spirit placement, only incense, a dish of water, dry rice, wine and dried meat, and betel nut — on the first and fifteenth of the month one dish of vegetables, with sweet fruits added; beyond this all is to be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: "For the three-day spirit placement, only incense, a dish of water, dry rice, wine and dried meat, and betel nut — on the first and fifteenth of the month one dish of vegetables, with sweet fruits added; beyond this all is to be reduced."

sentences.zh: 葬後除靈，可施吾常所乘輿扇傘。

translations.literal: "After burial when the spirit is removed, you may set out the carriage umbrella and fan I ordinarily used."
translations.idiomatic: "After burial when the spirit is removed, you may set out the carriage umbrella and fan I ordinarily used."

sentences.zh: 朔望時節，席地香火、盤水、酒脯、乾飯、檳榔便足。

translations.literal: "On the first and fifteenth and at seasonal festivals, incense on the ground, a dish of water, wine and dried meat, dry rice, and betel nut will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: "On the first and fifteenth and at seasonal festivals, incense on the ground, a dish of water, wine and dried meat, dry rice, and betel nut will suffice."

sentences.zh: 棺器及墓中勿用餘物為後患也。

translations.literal: "In the coffin fittings and tomb use no surplus goods that may become a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: "In the coffin fittings and tomb use no surplus goods that may become a later trouble."

sentences.zh: 朝服之外，唯下鐵環刀一口。

translations.literal: "Beyond court dress, only place one iron-ringed knife below."
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond court dress, only place one iron-ringed knife below."

sentences.zh: 作塚勿令深，一一依格，莫過度也。

translations.literal: "In building the tomb do not make it deep; follow regulations in every respect and do not exceed the standard."
translations.idiomatic: "In building the tomb do not make it deep; follow regulations in every respect and do not exceed the standard."

sentences.zh: 後堂樓可安佛，供養外國二僧，餘皆如舊。

translations.literal: "The rear hall tower may house a Buddha image and support two foreign monks; the rest remains as before."
translations.idiomatic: "The rear hall tower may house a Buddha image and support two foreign monks; the rest remains as before."

sentences.zh: 與汝遊戲後堂船乘，吾所乘牛馬，送二宮及司徒。

translations.literal: "The rear-hall boats in which I played with you, and the cattle and horses I rode — send them to the Two Palaces and the Secretariat Director."
translations.idiomatic: "The rear-hall boats in which I played with you, and the cattle and horses I rode — send them to the Two Palaces and the Secretariat Director."

sentences.zh: 服飾衣裘，悉為功德。

translations.literal: "Garments, ornaments, and furs — all are to be dedicated as meritorious works."
translations.idiomatic: "Garments, ornaments, and furs — all are to be dedicated as meritorious works."

sentences.zh: 」子廉等號泣奉行。

translations.literal: " Zilian and the others wailed and carried out his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: " Zilian and the others wailed and carried out his instructions.

sentences.zh: 武帝哀痛特至，蔬食積旬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's grief was exceptionally deep; he ate only vegetables for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's grief was exceptionally deep; he ate only vegetables for many days.

sentences.zh: 太官朝夕送祭奠，敕王融為銘，云：「半嶽摧峰，中河墜月。

translations.literal: The Imperial Kitchen sent offerings morning and evening; the emperor ordered Wang Rong to compose an inscription, which read: "Half the mountain's peak is shattered; mid-river the moon has fallen."
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Kitchen sent offerings morning and evening; the emperor ordered Wang Rong to compose an inscription, which read, "Half the mountain's peak is shattered; mid-river the moon has fallen."

sentences.zh: 」帝流涕曰：「此正吾所欲言也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and said: "This is precisely what I wished to say."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept and said, "This is precisely what I wished to say."

sentences.zh: 至其年十二月，乃舉樂宴朝臣。

translations.literal: Only in the twelfth month of that year did he raise music and feast the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the twelfth month of that year did he raise music and feast the court ministers.

sentences.zh: 樂始舉，上便歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: As soon as the music began, the emperor sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the music began, the emperor sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 嶷薨後，第庫無見錢，武帝敕貨雜物服飾得數百萬，起集善寺，月給第見錢百萬，至上崩乃省。

translations.literal: After Luan's death the mansion treasury had no cash on hand; Emperor Wu ordered the sale of miscellaneous goods and ornaments, obtaining several million, and built Jishan Temple; each month he granted the mansion a million in cash — this was discontinued only when the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan's death the mansion treasury had no cash on hand; Emperor Wu ordered the sale of miscellaneous goods and ornaments, obtaining several million, and built Jishan Temple; each month he granted the mansion a million in cash — this was discontinued only when the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 嶷性泛愛，不樂聞人過失，左右投書相告，置靴中，竟不視，取火焚之。

translations.literal: Luan was by nature broadly loving and did not enjoy hearing of others' faults; when attendants submitted letters informing on one another, he placed them in his boot, never looked at them, and burned them in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was by nature broadly loving and did not enjoy hearing of others' faults; when attendants submitted letters informing on one another, he placed them in his boot, never looked at them, and burned them in the fire.

sentences.zh: 齋庫失火，燒荊州還資，評直三千餘萬，主局各杖數十而已。

translations.literal: The fasting-storehouse caught fire and burned the goods Luan had brought back from Jingzhou, assessed at more than thirty million; the chief clerks each received only several dozen strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting-storehouse caught fire and burned the goods Luan had brought back from Jingzhou, assessed at more than thirty million; the chief clerks each received only several dozen strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 嶷薨後，忽見形于沈文季曰：「我未應便死，皇太子加膏中十一種藥，使我癰不差，湯中復加藥一種，使利不斷。

translations.literal: After Luan's death he suddenly appeared in form to Shen Wenji and said: "I ought not to have died so soon — the Crown Prince added eleven kinds of medicine to the ointment, so my abscess would not heal; in the decoction he added another medicine, so my diarrhea would not stop."
translations.idiomatic: After Luan's death he suddenly appeared in form to Shen Wenji and said, "I ought not to have died so soon — the Crown Prince added eleven kinds of medicine to the ointment, so my abscess would not heal; in the decoction he added another medicine, so my diarrhea would not stop."

sentences.zh: 吾已訴先帝，先帝許還東邸，當判此事。

translations.literal: "I have already appealed to the late emperor; the late emperor has permitted me to return to the Eastern Mansion to judge this matter."
translations.idiomatic: "I have already appealed to the late emperor; the late emperor has permitted me to return to the Eastern Mansion to judge this matter."

sentences.zh: 」因胸中出青紙文書示文季曰：「與卿少舊，因卿呈上。

translations.literal: " He then produced a blue-paper document from his breast and showed Wenji: "We were old acquaintances in youth — through you I present this above."
translations.idiomatic: " He then produced a blue-paper document from his breast and showed Wenji, "We were old acquaintances in youth — through you I present this above."

sentences.zh: 」俄失所在。

translations.literal: " Shortly he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly he vanished.

sentences.zh: 文季秘而不傳，甚懼此事，少時太子薨。

translations.literal: Wenji kept it secret and did not transmit it, greatly fearing this matter; before long the Crown Prince died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji kept it secret and did not transmit it, greatly fearing this matter; before long the Crown Prince died.

sentences.zh: 又嘗見形於第後園，乘腰輿，指麾處分，呼直兵，直兵無手板，左右授一玉手板與之，謂曰：「橘樹一株死，可覓補之。

translations.literal: He also once appeared in form in the rear garden of the mansion, riding a waist carriage, directing and disposing affairs, calling the guards — the guards had no writing tablets, so attendants handed him a jade tablet and he said: "One orange tree has died — find a replacement."
translations.idiomatic: He also once appeared in form in the rear garden of the mansion, riding a waist carriage, directing affairs, calling the guards — the guards had no writing tablets, so attendants handed him a jade tablet and he said, "One orange tree has died — find a replacement."

sentences.zh: 」因出後園合，直兵倒地，仍失手板。

translations.literal: " He then went out through the rear garden gate; the guard collapsed to the ground and dropped the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went out through the rear garden gate; the guard collapsed to the ground and dropped the tablet.

sentences.zh: 群吏中南陽樂藹、彭城劉繪、吳郡張稷，最被親禮。

translations.literal: Among his staff, Yue Ai of Nanyang, Liu Hui of Pengcheng, and Zhang Ji of Wu Commandery were most favored with intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Among his staff, Yue Ai of Nanyang, Liu Hui of Pengcheng, and Zhang Ji of Wu Commandery were most favored with intimate courtesy.

sentences.zh: 藹與竟陵王子良箋，欲率荊、江、湘三州僚吏建碑，托中書侍郎劉繪營辦。

translations.literal: Ai wrote to Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, wishing to lead the officials of the three provinces Jing, Jiang, and Xiang to erect a stele, entrusting Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Liu Hui to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: Ai wrote to Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, wishing to lead the officials of the three provinces Jing, Jiang, and Xiang to erect a stele, entrusting Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Liu Hui to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 藹又與右率沈約書，請為文。

translations.literal: Ai also wrote to Right Commander Shen Yue, requesting him to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Ai also wrote to Right Commander Shen Yue, requesting him to compose the text.

sentences.zh: 約答曰：「郭有道漢末之匹夫，非蔡伯喈不足以偶三絕。

translations.literal: Yue replied: "Guo Youdao was a common man of late Han — without Cai Yong he would not have been worthy of the three perfections."
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied, "Guo Youdao was a common man of late Han — without Cai Yong he would not have been worthy of the three perfections."

sentences.zh: 謝安石素族之台輔，時無麗藻，迄乃有碑無文。

translations.literal: "Xie Anshi was a minister from an old family, yet in his time there was no fine literary talent — in the end there was a stele but no inscription."
translations.idiomatic: "Xie Anshi was a minister from an old family, yet in his time there was no fine literary talent — in the end there was a stele but no inscription."

sentences.zh: 況文獻王冠冕彝倫，儀刑宇內，自非一代辭宗，難或與此。

translations.literal: "How much more Prince Wenxian, who crowns the moral order and is the model within the realm — unless one were a literary master of an age, it would be hard to match this."
translations.idiomatic: "How much more Prince Wenxian, who crowns the moral order and is the model within the realm — unless one were a literary master of an age, it would be hard to match this."

sentences.zh: 約閭閈鄙人，名不入第，欻酬今旨，便是以禮許人，聞命慚顏，已不覺汗之沾背也。

translations.literal: "Yue is a rustic from the lanes, his name not entered in the registers — suddenly to answer this commission would be to grant a man by courtesy alone; hearing the command I blush with shame, already feeling sweat soak my back."
translations.idiomatic: "I am a rustic from the lanes, my name not entered in the registers — suddenly to answer this commission would be to grant a man by courtesy alone; hearing the command I blush with shame, already feeling sweat soak my back."

sentences.zh: 」建武中，第二子子恪托約及太子詹事孔珪為文。

translations.literal: " In the Jianwu era, the second son Zike entrusted Yue and the Heir Apparent's Household Mentor Kong Gui to compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Jianwu era, the second son Zike entrusted Yue and the Heir Apparent's Household Mentor Kong Gui to compose the text.

sentences.zh: 子廉字景藹。

translations.literal: Zilian, style name Jing'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian, whose style name was Jing'ai.

sentences.zh: 初，嶷養魚復侯子響為嗣子，子廉封永新侯，子響還本。

translations.literal: Initially Luan adopted Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, as heir; Zilian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin, and Zixiang returned to his original line.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Luan adopted Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, as heir; Zilian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin, and Zixiang returned to his original line.

sentences.zh: 子廉為世子，位淮陵太守，太子中舍人，前將軍，善撫諸弟。

translations.literal: Zilian became heir, holding the posts of Administrator of Huailing, Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Forward General; he was skilled in caring for his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian became heir, holding the posts of Administrator of Huailing, Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Forward General; he was skilled in caring for his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，贈侍中，諡哀世子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died; posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, posthumous title Lamented Heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died; posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the posthumous title Lamented Heir.

sentences.zh: 子元琳嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuanlin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanlin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 梁武受禪，詔曰：「豫章王元琳、故竟陵王昭胄子同，齊氏宗國，高、武嫡胤，宜祚井邑，以傳於後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the abdication, an edict said: "Prince of Yuzhang Yuanlin and Zitong, son of the late Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou — clansmen of the Qi house, legitimate descendants of Gao and Wu — should receive fiefs and towns to transmit to posterity."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the abdication, an edict said, "Prince of Yuzhang Yuanlin and Zitong, son of the late Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou — clansmen of the Qi house, legitimate descendants of Gao and Wu — should receive fiefs and towns to transmit to posterity."

sentences.zh: 降封新淦侯。」

translations.literal: "They were demoted and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan."
translations.idiomatic: "They were demoted and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan."

sentences.zh: 子廉弟子恪字景沖，永明中，以王子封南康縣侯。

translations.literal: Zilian's younger brother's son Zike, style name Jingchong, in the Yongming era was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang County by virtue of princely birth.
translations.idiomatic: Zilian's younger brother's son Zike, whose style name was Jingchong, in the Yongming era was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang County by virtue of princely birth.

sentences.zh: 年十二，和從兄司徒竟陵王子良高松賦，衛軍王儉見而奇之。

translations.literal: At age twelve he composed a rhapsody on lofty pines with his cousin Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, Grand Tutor of the Secretariat; Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian saw it and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At age twelve he composed a rhapsody on lofty pines with his cousin Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, Grand Tutor of the Secretariat; Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian saw it and marveled.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he became Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era he became Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及大司馬王敬則於會稽反，奉子恪為名，而子恪奔走，未知所在。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Wang Jingze rebelled at Kuaiji, he used Zike's name as a banner, while Zike fled and his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Wang Jingze rebelled at Kuaiji, he used Zike's name as a banner, while Zike fled and his whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光勸上並誅高、武諸子孫，於是並敕竟陵王昭胄等六十餘人入永福省，令太醫煮椒二斛，並命辦數十具棺材，謂舍人沈徽孚曰：「椒熟則一時賜死。

translations.literal: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang urged the emperor to execute together all descendants of Gao and Wu; thereupon more than sixty persons including Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou were ordered into Yongfu Palace, the Imperial Physician told to boil two hu of pepper, and several dozen coffins ordered prepared; he told Attendant Shen Huifu: "When the pepper is cooked, grant death all at once."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang urged the emperor to execute together all descendants of Gao and Wu; thereupon more than sixty persons including Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou were ordered into Yongfu Palace, the Imperial Physician told to boil two hu of pepper, and several dozen coffins ordered prepared; he told Attendant Shen Huifu, "When the pepper is cooked, grant death all at once."

sentences.zh: 」期三更當殺之。

translations.literal: " The time was set for the third watch of the night when they were to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: " The time was set for the third watch of the night when they were to be killed.

sentences.zh: 會上暫臥，主書單景雋啟依旨斃之，徽孚堅執曰：「事須更審。

translations.literal: The emperor was briefly resting; Chief Clerk Shan Jingjun reported that according to the order they should be put to death. Huifu firmly held: "The matter must be reviewed again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was briefly resting; Chief Clerk Shan Jingjun reported that according to the order they should be put to death. Huifu firmly held, "The matter must be reviewed again."

sentences.zh: 」爾夕三更，子恪徒跣奔至建陽門。

translations.literal: " That evening at the third watch, Zike ran barefoot to Jiayang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " That evening at the third watch, Zike ran barefoot to Jiayang Gate.

sentences.zh: 上聞驚覺曰：「故當未賜諸侯命邪？

translations.literal: Hearing this, the startled emperor awoke and said: "Surely the order to execute the princes has not yet been given?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the startled emperor awoke and said, "Surely the order to execute the princes has not yet been given?"

sentences.zh: 」徽孚以答。

translations.literal: " Huifu answered accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " Huifu answered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 上撫床曰：「遙光幾誤人事。

translations.literal: The emperor struck the bed and said: "Yaoguang nearly ruined the affair of state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor struck the bed and said, "Yaoguang nearly ruined the affair of state."

sentences.zh: 」及見子恪，顧問流涕，諸侯悉賜供饌。

translations.literal: " When he saw Zike, he looked back and wept; all the princes were granted provisions.
translations.idiomatic: " When he saw Zike, he looked back and wept; all the princes were granted provisions.

sentences.zh: 以子恪為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He appointed Zike as Senior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zike was appointed Senior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，為侍中。

translations.literal: When Donghun ascended the throne, [he] became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，為相國諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, [he] became Consulting Military Advisor to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing, he served as Consulting Military Advisor to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，降爵為子，位司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Liang Tianjian, [his] rank was reduced to Baron, [and he] held the post of Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Liang's Tianjian era, his noble rank was reduced to baron, and he was appointed Left Chief Administrator under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子恪與弟子范等嘗因事入謝，梁武帝在文德殿引見，謂曰：「夫天下之寶，本是公器，苟無期運，雖有項籍之力，終亦敗亡。

translations.literal: Zike together with his younger brothers Zifan and others once entered on some matter to offer thanks; Emperor Wu of Liang received them in audience at the Wende Hall and said to them: "The treasure of All Under Heaven is fundamentally a public vessel; if there is no destined fortune, even with the strength of Xiang Yu, one will ultimately fail and perish.
translations.idiomatic: Zike and his younger brothers Zifan and others once came to court to offer thanks on a particular matter. Emperor Wu of Liang received them at the Wende Hall and said: "The empire is a public trust. Without the mandate of fate, even a man as strong as Xiang Yu is doomed to fail in the end.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武為性猜忌，兄弟粗有令名者，無不因事鴆毒，所遺唯景和。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song was by nature suspicious and jealous; among the brothers who roughly had fine reputations, none failed to be poisoned on some pretext—the sole survivor was Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song was mistrustful by nature. Every brother who had earned even a modest reputation was eventually poisoned on some pretext; only Prince Jinghe was spared.

sentences.zh: 至朝臣之中疑有天命而致害者，枉濫相繼。

translations.literal: As for those among court ministers suspected of possessing the Mandate of Heaven and thus harmed, wrongful excess followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At court, officials suspected of bearing the Mandate of Heaven were likewise destroyed in an unending succession of unjust killings.

sentences.zh: 于時雖疑卿祖，無如之何。

translations.literal: At that time, though [he] suspected your grandfather, there was nothing to be done about it.
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfather aroused his suspicions even then, yet there was nothing he could do about it.

sentences.zh: 如宋明帝本為庸常被免，豈疑得全。

translations.literal: Take Emperor Ming of Song: he was originally a common mediocrity and was dismissed—could suspicion have allowed him to survive intact?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Emperor Ming of Song: he was an unremarkable man who had been dismissed from office—how could mere suspicion have kept him alive?

sentences.zh: 又復我于時已年二歲，彼豈知我應有今日。

translations.literal: Moreover, I was already two years old at the time—how could he have known that I was destined for what I have today?
translations.idiomatic: And I was only two years old then. How could he have foreseen that I would come to this?

sentences.zh: 當知有天命者非人所害，害亦不能得。

translations.literal: One should know that one whom Heaven has destined cannot be harmed by men; even if harmed, [they] cannot be gotten.
translations.idiomatic: A man favored by Heaven cannot be destroyed by human hands; attempts to kill him will fail.

sentences.zh: 我初平建康城，朝廷內外皆勸我云：'時代革異，物心須一，宜行處分。

translations.literal: When I first pacified Jiankang, those inside and outside the court all urged me, saying: 'The age has changed, the hearts of all must be united—proper measures should be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When I first seized Jiankang, court and country alike urged me: 'The dynasty has changed; the people's loyalties must be consolidated. You ought to take decisive action.

sentences.zh: '我于時依此而行，誰謂不可？

translations.literal: ' If I had acted accordingly at the time, who would say it was wrong?
translations.idiomatic: 'Had I followed that advice, who could have faulted me?

sentences.zh: 政言江左以來，代謝必相誅戮，此是傷于和氣，國祚例不靈長。
