translations.literal: It is precisely because, since the establishment of the Eastern Jin, each dynastic change has necessarily involved mutual slaughter that harmony is injured and imperial fortunes as a rule do not endure long.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that ever since the Eastern Jin, every dynastic transition has been marked by mutual slaughter—a habit that destroys harmony and ensures that no realm lasts long.

sentences.zh: 此是一義。

translations.literal: This is one principle.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first consideration.

sentences.zh: 二者，齊、梁雖曰革代，義異往時。

translations.literal: Second, though Qi and Liang are called a dynastic change, the principle differs from former times.
translations.idiomatic: Second, although Qi gave way to Liang, the circumstances differ from previous changes of dynasty.

sentences.zh: 我與卿兄弟宗屬未遠，卿勿言兄弟是親，人家兄弟自有周旋者不周旋者，況五服之屬邪？

translations.literal: My clan relationship with you brothers is not distant. Do not say that brothers are kin—in every family some brothers are close and some are not; how much more so for relatives within the five degrees of mourning?
translations.idiomatic: I am not far removed from your branch of the clan. Do not assume that blood ties alone guarantee loyalty—even among brothers, some remain close and some do not; how much less can one rely on kinship within the five degrees of mourning?

sentences.zh: 齊業之初，亦是甘苦共嘗，腹心在我，卿兄弟年少，理當不悉。

translations.literal: At the founding of Qi's enterprise, we likewise shared bitter and sweet together; those closest to my heart were with me—you brothers were young and naturally ought not to know this fully.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi enterprise was first launched, we shared hardship and triumph alike; my inner circle stood with me. You were young then, and naturally would not know this well.

sentences.zh: 我與卿兄弟便是情同一家，豈當都不念此，作行路事。

translations.literal: My feelings toward you brothers are as one family—how could I fail to keep this in mind and treat you as strangers on the road?
translations.idiomatic: I regard you as family in every meaningful sense. How could I forget that and treat you as strangers?

sentences.zh: 此是二義。

translations.literal: This is the second principle.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second consideration.

sentences.zh: 且建武屠滅卿門，我起義兵，非惟自雪門恥，亦是為卿兄弟報仇。

translations.literal: Moreover, during Jianwu [your] clan was slaughtered; I raised righteous troops—not only to wipe away my own family's shame, but also to avenge you brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwu reign massacred your house, I raised an army—not only to redeem my own family's honor, but to avenge your brothers as well.

sentences.zh: 卿若能在建武、永元之時撥亂反正，我雖起樊、鄧，豈得不釋戈推奉。

translations.literal: If you had been able to restore order amid the chaos during Jianwu and Yongyuan, even though I rose from Fan and Deng, how could I have failed to lay down my weapons and defer to you?
translations.idiomatic: Had you restored order during the Jianwu and Yongyuan reigns, I would have laid down my arms and submitted to you—even though I had risen from Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 我今為卿報仇，且時代革異，望卿兄弟盡節報我耳。

translations.literal: Now I have avenged you, and as the age has changed, I only hope you brothers will devote yourselves in return to me.
translations.idiomatic: I have already avenged your wrongs. With the change of dynasty, I ask only that you and your brothers serve me with wholehearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 且我自藉喪亂，代明帝家天下，不取卿家天下。

translations.literal: Moreover, I have taken the realm through the chaos in place of the Ming Emperor's house—I have not taken your family's realm.
translations.idiomatic: I seized the realm in the turmoil that followed the Ming Emperor's fall; I did not take it from your house.

sentences.zh: 昔劉子輿自稱成帝子，光武言：'假使成帝更生，天下亦不復可得，況子輿乎？

translations.literal: Formerly Liu Ziyu claimed to be the son of Emperor Cheng; Emperor Guangwu said: 'Even if Emperor Cheng were reborn, the realm could not be regained—how much less so for Ziyu?
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Ziyu claimed to be the son of Emperor Cheng. Emperor Guangwu replied: 'Even if Emperor Cheng himself returned to life, the realm could not be recovered—what chance had Ziyu?

sentences.zh: '梁初人勸我相誅滅者，我答之猶如向言：'若苟有天命，非我所殺，若其無運，何忽行此，政是示無度量。

translations.literal: ' At the founding of Liang, those who urged me to exterminate one another, I answered as I just said: 'If there is truly the Mandate of Heaven, it is not I who could kill them; if there is no destined fortune, why suddenly do this—it would only show lack of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: 'When Liang was founded, some urged me to slaughter the former rulers' kin. I answered as I have just said: 'If Heaven has chosen them, I cannot kill them; if they lack destiny, what need is there for slaughter? That would only show petty vindictiveness.

sentences.zh: '曹志親是魏武帝孫，入事晉武，為晉室忠臣。

translations.literal: ' Cao Zhi was by kinship a grandson of Emperor Wu of Wei; he entered service under Emperor Wu of Jin and became a loyal minister of the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: 'Cao Zhi was a grandson of Emperor Wu of Wei; he entered the service of Emperor Wu of Jin and proved a loyal minister of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 此即卿事例。

translations.literal: This is precisely your precedent.
translations.idiomatic: You should take him as your model.

sentences.zh: 卿是宗室，情義異他，方坦然相期，小待自當知我寸心。

translations.literal: You are of the imperial clan; your bond of sentiment and duty differs from others. I frankly look forward to this—wait a little and you will naturally know the depths of my heart.
translations.idiomatic: As members of the imperial clan, your tie to me is unlike that of ordinary subjects. I speak to you openly now; in time you will understand my true intentions.

sentences.zh: 」又文獻王時內齋直帳閹人趙叔祖，天監初入台為齋帥在壽光省。

translations.literal: " Moreover, during Prince Wenxian's time the eunuch Zhao Shuzu served in the inner fasting-hall tent-guard; at the beginning of Tianjian he entered the palace platform as fasting-hall chief in the Shouguang office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also mentioned that during Prince Wenxian's reign the eunuch Zhao Shuzu had served in the inner fasting hall. At the start of Tianjian, Zhao entered the palace administration as head of the fasting hall in the Shouguang office.

sentences.zh: 武帝呼問曰：「汝比見北第諸郎不？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu summoned and questioned him, saying: "Have you lately seen the young lords of the Northern Residence?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him and asked: "Have you recently seen the young lords of the Northern Residence?

sentences.zh: 若見道我此意：今日雖是革代，情同一家；

translations.literal: If you see them, convey my meaning: though today is a change of dynasty, our feelings are as one family;
translations.idiomatic: If you do, tell them what I mean: though the dynasty has changed, we are as one family in spirit;

sentences.zh: 但今磐石未立，所以未得用諸郎。

translations.literal: but at present the foundation stone is not yet established, and therefore I have not yet been able to employ the young lords.
translations.idiomatic: but my foundation is not yet secure, and that is why I cannot yet appoint them to office.

sentences.zh: 非唯在我未宜，我亦是欲使諸郎得得安耳。

translations.literal: It is not only that it would be inappropriate for me—I also wish to let the young lords live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that the time is not right for me; I also wish to keep them safe and at ease.

sentences.zh: 但閉門高枕，後自當見我心。

translations.literal: Only close your doors and rest your head on your pillow—in time you will naturally see my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Let them shut their doors and live in peace; in time they will see what I truly intend.

sentences.zh: 」叔祖即出具宣敕意。

translations.literal: " Shuzu immediately went out and proclaimed the import of the imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shuzu went out at once and delivered the Emperor's message.

sentences.zh: 子恪普通三年累遷都官尚書，四年轉吏部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong, Zike was successively promoted to Minister of Justice; in the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Putong, Zike rose to Minister of Justice; the following year he was transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，出為吳郡太守，卒官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he went out as Governor of Wu Commandery and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, he was appointed Governor of Wu Commandery and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Baron Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Baron Gong.

sentences.zh: 子恪兄弟十六人併入梁，有文學者子恪、子質、子顯、子雲、子暉。

translations.literal: Sixteen brothers of Zike all entered Liang together; those with literary accomplishment were Zike, Zizhi, Zixian, Ziyun, and Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: All sixteen of Zike's brothers entered Liang together. Those distinguished in letters were Zike, Zizhi, Zixian, Ziyun, and Zihui.

sentences.zh: 子恪常謂所親曰：「文史之事，諸弟備之矣，不煩吾復牽率。

translations.literal: Zike often said to those close to him: "Matters of literature and history—my younger brothers have them fully covered; no need for me again to lead and drag along.
translations.idiomatic: Zike often told his intimates: "My younger brothers have literature and history well in hand; there is no need for me to take the lead again.

sentences.zh: 但退食自公，無過足矣。」

translations.literal: Only to withdraw after eating from public duty without fault is enough."
translations.idiomatic: It is enough for me to leave office after my meal without scandal."

sentences.zh: 子恪亦涉學，頗屬文，隨棄其本，故不傳文集。

translations.literal: Zike also dabbled in learning and rather often composed texts, but discarded his drafts as he went; therefore no collected works were transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zike too had some learning and wrote occasional pieces, but he discarded his drafts as he went, so no collected works survive.

sentences.zh: 子操弟子范字景則。

translations.literal: Zifan, son of Zicao, styled Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan, son of Zicao, styled himself Jingze.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中封祁陽縣侯，拜太子洗馬。

translations.literal: During Qi Yongming, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiyang County and appointed Groom of the Crown Prince's Stables.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming reign of Qi, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiyang and appointed Groom of the Crown Prince's Stables.

sentences.zh: 天監初降爵為子，位司徒主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, his rank was reduced to Baron, and he held the post of Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, his noble rank was reduced to baron, and he served as Chief Clerk under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁所生母憂去職。

translations.literal: Upon the mourning for his birth mother, he left his post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his biological mother died.

sentences.zh: 子範有孝性，居喪以毀聞。

translations.literal: Zifan had a filial nature; during mourning he was renowned for emaciating himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan was filial by nature; his grief during mourning was so intense that it became well known.

sentences.zh: 服闋，累遷大司馬南平王從事中郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was successively promoted to Attendant Officer to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, he rose to Attendant Officer under the Grand Marshal, Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 王愛文學士，子范偏被恩遇，常曰：「此宗室奇才也。

translations.literal: The prince loved literary scholars; Zifan was especially favored and often said: "This is an extraordinary talent among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The prince favored men of letters and showed Zifan particular favor, often declaring: "Here is a rare genius among the imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 」使制千字文，其辭甚美。

translations.literal: " He had him compose a Thousand-Character Text; its wording was extremely fine.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned Zifan to compose a Thousand-Character Text, and the text was beautifully wrought.

sentences.zh: 王命記室蔡薳注釋之。

translations.literal: The prince ordered his secretariat officer Cai Wei to annotate and explain it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered his secretariat officer Cai Wei to annotate it.

sentences.zh: 自是府中文筆皆使具草。

translations.literal: From then on, all official writing in the princely establishment was assigned to him for drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, all official documents in the prince's household were entrusted to him for drafting.

sentences.zh: 後為臨賀王正德長史。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Administrator to Prince Zhengde of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Administrator to Prince Zhengde of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 正德遷丹陽尹，復為正德信威長史，領尹丞。

translations.literal: When Zhengde was transferred to Governor of Danyang, [Zifan] again became Chief Administrator of Trust and Prestige to Zhengde, concurrently serving as Assistant Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde was appointed Governor of Danyang, Zifan again served as his Chief Administrator of Trust and Prestige, concurrently holding the post of Assistant Governor.

sentences.zh: 曆官十餘年，不出蕃府，而諸弟並登顯列，意不能平。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years in office, he never left the princely establishment, while all his younger brothers simultaneously reached prominent ranks—his mind could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he remained within princely service while his younger brothers all rose to high office; he could not reconcile himself to this.

sentences.zh: 及是為到府箋曰：「上蕃首僚，於茲再忝，河南雌伏，自此重叨。

translations.literal: On this occasion he submitted to the princely residence a memorial saying: "As chief officer of the foremost princely establishment, here again I am doubly honored; like the hen of Henan crouching in submission, from this point I again receive undeserved favor.
translations.idiomatic: On this appointment he submitted a memorial to the princely residence: "As chief officer of the foremost princely establishment, I am once again undeservedly honored; like a hen crouching in Henan, I again receive a favor I have scarcely earned.

sentences.zh: 老少異時，盛衰殊日，雖佩恩寵，還羞年鬢。

translations.literal: Old and young differ in their times; prosperity and decline fall on different days—though I bear favor and grace, I still feel shame at my age and gray hair.
translations.idiomatic: Youth and age belong to different seasons; rise and fall come on different days. Though still favored, I am ashamed of my advancing years and gray hair.

sentences.zh: 」子范少與弟子顯、子雲才名略相比，而風采容止不逮，故宦途有優劣。

translations.literal: " Zifan in his youth was roughly comparable in talent and reputation with his younger brother Zixian and Ziyun, but in bearing and deportment he did not match them; therefore their official careers had superior and inferior [outcomes].
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zifan was nearly the equal of his younger brothers Zixian and Ziyun in talent and reputation, but his presence and bearing fell short of theirs, and their careers accordingly diverged in success.

sentences.zh: 每讀漢書杜緩傳云：「六弟五人至大官，唯中弟欽官不至，最知名。

translations.literal: Whenever he read the Biography of Du Huan in the Book of Han, which says: "Of six brothers, five reached high office; only the middle brother Qin did not attain office, yet was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read the Biography of Du Huan in the Book of Han—"Of six brothers, five rose to high office; only the middle brother Qin did not, yet he was the most famous

sentences.zh: 」常吟諷之，以況己也。

translations.literal: " he would often chant and recite it, using it to compare with himself.
translations.idiomatic: —he would recite the passage to himself, taking it as a mirror of his own case.

sentences.zh: 後為秘書監。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 簡文即位，召為光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, [Zifan] was summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with gold seal and purple ribbon added.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen succeeded to the throne, Zifan was summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted a gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 以逼賊不拜。

translations.literal: Because the rebels were pressing close, he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebels pressing in, he declined to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 其年葬簡皇后，使制哀策，文理哀切。

translations.literal: That year, at the burial of Empress Jian, he was ordered to compose the mourning encomium; its literary form and reasoning were mournful and piercing.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when Empress Jian was buried, he was commissioned to write the mourning encomium; the text was eloquent and deeply mournful.

sentences.zh: 帝謂武林侯蕭諮曰：「此段莊陵萬事零落，唯哀冊尚有典刑。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Marquis Wulin Xiao Zi: "At this stretch of Zhuangling, all things have fallen into ruin; only the mourning encomium still preserves the classic model.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Marquis Wulin Xiao Zi: "At Zhuangling everything has been laid waste; only this mourning encomium still upholds the ancient standard.

sentences.zh: 」敕賚米千石。

translations.literal: " An edict awarded him a thousand shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded by imperial edict with a thousand shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 子范無居宅，尋卒於招提寺僧房。

translations.literal: Zifan had no residence; soon afterward he died in a monk's cell at Zhaoti Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan owned no home and soon died in a monk's cell at Zhaoti Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊平，元帝追贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Emperor Yuan posthumously awarded him the post of Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, Emperor Yuan posthumously honored him as Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and gave him the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 前後文集三十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works before and after [his death] totaled thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works totaled thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子滂、確並少有文章，簡文在東宮時，嘗與邵陵王數諸蕭文士，滂、確並預焉。

translations.literal: Zibang and Que both in youth had literary composition; when Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace, he often gathered with Prince of Shaoling and several Xiao literary scholars—Zibang and Que both participated.
translations.idiomatic: Zibang and Que both showed literary talent from youth. When Jianwen was crown prince, he often gathered with Prince Shaoling and various Xiao men of letters; Zibang and Que both took part.

sentences.zh: 滂位中軍宣城王記室，先子範卒。

translations.literal: Zibang held the post of Secretariat Officer to Prince of Xuancheng of the Central Army; he died before Zifan.
translations.idiomatic: Zibang served as Secretariat Officer to Prince Xuancheng of the Central Army and died before Zifan.

sentences.zh: 確位司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Que held the post of Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Que served as Right Chief Administrator under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，入長安。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, [he] entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei conquered Jiangling, he was taken to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，留異反，陳寶應助之，又資周迪兵糧，出寇臨川，因逼建安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, Liu Yi rebelled; Chen Baoying assisted him, also supplying Zhou Di with troops and grain; [they] went out to raid Linchuan and thereby pressed upon Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng, Liu Yi rebelled. Chen Baoying aided him and supplied Zhou Di with troops and grain; the rebels raided Linchuan and pressed toward Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 幹單使臨郡，不能守，乃棄郡以避寶應。

translations.literal: Gan alone was sent to govern the commandery; unable to hold it, he abandoned the commandery to avoid Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was governing the commandery alone and could not hold it, so he abandoned his post to escape Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 時閩中宰守並受寶應署置，幹獨不屈，徙居郊野。

translations.literal: At the time the prefects and commandants of Minzhong all accepted appointments from Baoying; only Gan did not submit, and moved to dwell in the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prefects and commandants throughout Min all accepted appointments from Baoying, but Gan alone refused to submit and withdrew to live in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 及寶應平，都督章昭達以聞，文帝甚嘉之，超授五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When Baoying was pacified, Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda reported it; Emperor Wen greatly praised this and specially appointed [Gan] Minister of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoying was suppressed, Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda reported Gan's conduct to the throne. Emperor Wen greatly praised him and promoted him out of turn to Minister of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡靜子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Baron Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Baron Jing.

sentences.zh: 子顯字景陽，子范弟也。

translations.literal: Zixian, styled Jingyang, was the younger brother of Zifan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian, styled Jingyang, was Zifan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，嶷偏愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and intelligent; Luan especially loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, he was especially favored by Prince Luan.

sentences.zh: 七歲，封甯都縣侯，梁天監初，降為子。

translations.literal: At age seven, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningdu County; at the beginning of Liang Tianjian, [his rank] was reduced to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningdu; at the start of Liang's Tianjian era his rank was reduced to baron.

sentences.zh: 位太尉錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He held the post of Recording Affairs Military Advisor to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recording Affairs Military Advisor to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 子顯身長八尺，狀貌甚雅，好學，工屬文。

translations.literal: Zixian was eight chi in height, his appearance very refined; he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian stood eight chi tall, with a refined bearing; he loved learning and was adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 嘗著鴻序賦，尚書令沈約見而稱曰：「可謂明道之高致，蓋幽通之流也。

translations.literal: He once composed the "Preface to the Wild Goose" rhapsody; Minister of Works Shen Yue saw it and praised it, saying: "This may be called the lofty aspiration of one who illumines the Way—it belongs to the stream of those who penetrate the hidden.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote the rhapsody "Preface to the Wild Goose." When Minister of Works Shen Yue read it, he praised it, saying: "This is the lofty spirit of one who illumines the Way—it belongs among those who penetrate the hidden realms.

sentences.zh: 」又采眾家後漢考正同異，為一家之書。

translations.literal: " He also gathered various authors' accounts of the Later Han, examined and corrected agreements and differences, and made a book of one school.
translations.idiomatic: He also collated various accounts of the Later Han, reconciled their discrepancies, and produced a history in his own synthesis.

sentences.zh: 又啟撰齊史，書成表奏，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial to compile the History of Qi; when the book was completed he memorialized it, and an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to compile the History of Qi; when the work was finished he submitted it to the throne, and an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 累遷邵陵王友。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Companion to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Companion to Prince Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 後除黃門郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，遷長兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was transferred to Senior Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was promoted to Senior Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝雅愛子顯才，又嘉其容止吐納，每御筵侍坐，偏顧訪焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly loved Zixian's talent, and also admired his bearing and speech in conversation; whenever he held imperial banquets and [Zixian] attended seated, he especially turned to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly admired Zixian's talent and his bearing and conversation at court; whenever the Emperor held banquets and Zixian was in attendance, he would turn especially to question him.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容謂曰：「我造通史，此書若成，眾史可廢。

translations.literal: He once said to him at ease: "I am composing a Comprehensive History; if this book is completed, the various histories may be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to him in an unhurried tone: "I am composing a Comprehensive History. If this book is completed, all other histories may be set aside.

sentences.zh: 」子顯對曰：「仲尼贊易道，黜八索；

translations.literal: " Zixian replied: "Confucius praised the Way of the Changes and dismissed the Eight Cord Records;
translations.idiomatic: Zixian replied: "Confucius praised the Way of the Changes and dismissed the Eight Cord Records;

sentences.zh: 述職方，除九丘。

translations.literal: he set forth the Records of Duty and removed the Nine Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: he expounded the Records of Duty and abolished the Nine Mounds.

sentences.zh: 聖制符同，復在茲日。

translations.literal: The sage's design matches this—the same is true on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Your sage's design accords with his—the same holds true today.

sentences.zh: 」時以為名對。

translations.literal: " At the time this was considered a famous reply.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was considered a celebrated reply.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the third year, with his existing office he concurrently served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he concurrently served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 武帝制孝經義，未列學官，子顯在職，表置助教一人，生十人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu composed exegeses of the Classic of Filial Piety, but they had not yet been placed in the academic offices; while in office, Zixian memorialized to establish one assistant instructor and ten students.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had composed exegeses of the Classic of Filial Piety, but they had not yet been incorporated into the academic curriculum. While in office, Zixian petitioned to appoint one assistant instructor and ten students.

sentences.zh: 又啟撰武帝集並普通北伐記。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial to compile the Collected Works of Emperor Wu and the Record of the Putong Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to compile the Emperor's collected works and the Record of the Putong Northern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，加侍中，於學遞述武帝五經義，遷吏部尚書，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Rector of the Imperial Academy, with Palace Attendant added; at the academy he successively expounded the Emperor's exegeses of the Five Classics; he was transferred to Minister of Personnel, with Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Rector of the Imperial Academy with the additional title of Palace Attendant; at the academy he lectured on the Emperor's exegeses of the Five Classics in sequence. He was then transferred to Minister of Personnel while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子顯風神灑落，雍容閒雅，簡通賓客，不畏鬼神。

translations.literal: Zixian's bearing and spirit were free and unbound; dignified and easy in leisure; simple in receiving guests; unafraid of ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian carried himself with effortless grace—refined yet unhurried, plainspoken with guests, and utterly unafraid of ghosts or spirits.

sentences.zh: 性愛山水，為伐社文以見其志。

translations.literal: By nature he loved mountains and waters; he wrote an essay on destroying the village shrine to reveal his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved mountains and rivers by temperament, and wrote an essay denouncing the village shrine to declare where he stood.

sentences.zh: 飲酒數斗，頗負才氣。

translations.literal: He drank several pecks of wine and was quite proud of his talent and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink several pecks at a sitting and was rather full of literary pride.

sentences.zh: 及掌選，見九流賓客不與交言，但舉扇一撝而已，衣冠竊恨。

translations.literal: When he took charge of selection, upon seeing guests of the nine streams he would not exchange words, but merely lift his fan and wave it once; the gentry secretly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Once he oversaw appointments, he would not so much as speak to visitors of every stripe—only lift his fan in a dismissive wave—much to the quiet resentment of the official class.

sentences.zh: 然簡文素重其為人，在東宮時，每引與促宴。

translations.literal: Yet Jianwen had always valued his character; while in the Eastern Palace, he often invited him to intimate banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen, however, had long esteemed the man himself; during his years as heir, he repeatedly drew Zixian into close, convivial feasts.

sentences.zh: 子顯嘗起更衣，簡文謂坐客曰：「常聞異人間出，今日始見，知是蕭尚書。

translations.literal: Zixian once rose to change clothes; Jianwen said to the seated guests: "I have often heard that extraordinary men appear among the people; today I have at last seen one—I know it is Director Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Zixian rose to change clothes, Jianwen told those at table: "One often hears that remarkable men appear from time to time; today I have seen one at last—the Minister Xiao.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Grand Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 卒時年四十九，詔贈侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: At death he was forty-nine; an edict posthumously granted him Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine; the throne posthumously honored him with the titles Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及請諡，手敕曰：「恃才傲物，宜諡曰驕。

translations.literal: When a posthumous title was requested, an imperial hand-edict said: "Relying on talent and disdaining others—the posthumous title should be Arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When a posthumous name was sought, the Emperor wrote in his own hand: "Presuming on talent and looking down on the world—let his posthumous title be Arrogant.

sentences.zh: 」子顯嘗為自序，其略云：「余為邵陵王友，忝還京師，遠思前比，即楚之唐、宋，梁之嚴、鄒。

translations.literal: " Zixian once wrote a self-preface; the gist says: "I served as Companion to the Prince of Shaoling and was honored to return to the capital. Thinking back on my predecessors—in Chu there were Tang and Song; in Liang there are Yan and Zou.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixian once composed a preface to his own works, which in summary reads: "I served as Companion to the Prince of Shaoling and was fortunate to return to the capital. Looking to earlier exemplars—Tang and Song in Chu, Yan and Zou in Liang.

sentences.zh: 追尋平生，頗好辭藻，雖在名無成，求心已足。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my whole life, I have quite loved literary ornament; though I have achieved no fame in name, what my heart sought is already satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing my life, I have always loved fine language; though I have won no lasting renown, what my heart sought is already enough.

sentences.zh: 若乃登高目極，臨水送歸，風動春朝，月明秋夜，早雁初鸚，開花落葉，有來斯應，每不能已也。

translations.literal: When I climb high and gaze to the horizon, stand by water seeing off a return, feel wind stir on a spring morning, see moonlight on an autumn night, hear wild geese fly early and orioles first call, watch flowers open and leaves fall—when these come, response follows, and I can never restrain myself.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I climb high and look to the horizon, or stand by water bidding farewell; whether wind stirs on a spring morning or moonlight fills an autumn night; whether wild geese pass early or orioles first sing, flowers bloom or leaves fall—when such things arrive, I must answer in words, and cannot stop myself.

sentences.zh: 且前代賈、傅、崔、馬、邯鄲、繆、路之徒，並以文章顯，所以屢上歌頌，自比古人。

translations.literal: Moreover, men of former ages—Jia, Fu, Cui, Ma, Handan, Miao, Lu, and the like—all were distinguished by their writings; therefore I have repeatedly submitted songs of praise, comparing myself to the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Men of earlier times—Jia, Fu, Cui, Ma, Handan, Miao, Lu, and others—won fame through writing; so I too have often submitted panegyrics, measuring myself against the ancients.

sentences.zh: 天監十六年，始預九日朝宴，稠人廣坐，獨受旨云：'今雲物甚美，卿將不斐然賦詩。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian, I first participated in the Double Ninth court banquet; amid a dense crowd and broad seating, I alone received the command: 'The clouds and scenery today are exceedingly fine—you surely will compose an outstanding poem.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian I first attended the Double Ninth court feast; in a hall crowded with guests, I alone received the command: 'The sky and landscape today are splendid—you will surely compose a fine poem.

sentences.zh: '詩既成，又降旨曰：'可謂才子。

translations.literal: ' When the poem was done, another command came down: 'One may truly call you a literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the poem was finished, another command followed: 'You may truly be called a man of letters.

sentences.zh: '餘退謂人曰：一顧之恩，非望而至，遂方賈誼何如哉，未易當也。

translations.literal: ' I withdrew and said to others: A single glance of favor, arriving unhoped-for—to be likened to Jia Yi! Not easy to live up to.
translations.idiomatic: ' I withdrew and told others: a single favor, unlooked-for, and then to be compared with Jia Yi—no easy burden to bear.

sentences.zh: 每有制作，特寡思功，須其自來，不以力構。

translations.literal: Whenever I have a composition, I put little deliberate effort into it; I must wait until it comes of itself—I do not construct it by force.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I write, I seldom labor at it; I wait until the words come on their own and do not force them into shape.

sentences.zh: 少來所為詩賦，則鴻序一作，體兼眾制，文備多方，頗為好事所傳，故虛聲易遠。

translations.literal: Of the poetry and rhapsodies I have written since youth, the Great Preface alone combines many forms and covers many aspects of style; it is much circulated among enthusiasts, so an empty reputation travels easily.
translations.idiomatic: Among the poems and rhapsodies I wrote in youth, the Great Preface alone embraces many genres and many modes of expression; enthusiasts spread it widely, so hollow fame travels far.

sentences.zh: 」子顯所著後漢書一百卷，齊書六十卷，普通北伐記五卷，貴儉傳三卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: " Zixian's writings included: History of the Later Han in one hundred juan, History of Qi in sixty juan, Record of the Putong Northern Expedition in five juan, Biographies of Frugal Worthies in three juan, and Collected Writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixian authored a History of the Later Han in one hundred juan, a History of Qi in sixty juan, a Record of the Putong Northern Expedition in five juan, Biographies of Frugal Worthies in three juan, and Collected Writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子序、愷並少知名。

translations.literal: Zixu and Kai were both known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zixu and Kai were both celebrated while still young.

sentences.zh: 序太清中位中庶子，卒。

translations.literal: Xu, during the Taqing era, held the post of Vice Director of the Left and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu served as Vice Director of the Left during the Taqing era and died in office.

sentences.zh: 愷太子家令。

translations.literal: Kai was Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Kai served as Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 愷才學譽望，時論以方其父。

translations.literal: Kai's talent, learning, and reputation led contemporaries to compare him to his father.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's learning and standing were such that contemporaries ranked him alongside his father.

sentences.zh: 簡文在東宮早引接之。

translations.literal: Jianwen, while in the Eastern Palace, had early taken him up and drawn him close.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir, Jianwen had long since taken Kai under his wing.

sentences.zh: 時中庶子謝嘏出守建安，于宣猷堂餞飲，並召時才賦詩，同用十五劇韻。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Director Xie Ga was going out to govern Jian'an; at Xuanyou Hall a farewell banquet was held, and contemporary talents were summoned to compose poetry, all using the same fifteen difficult rhymes.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director Xie Ga was sent out to govern Jian'an, a farewell feast was held at Xuanyou Hall; the day's talents were called to compose poems, all bound to the same fifteen difficult rhymes.

sentences.zh: 愷詩先就，其辭又美。

translations.literal: Kai's poem was finished first, and its wording was also fine.
translations.idiomatic: Kai finished first, and his lines were the finest as well.

sentences.zh: 簡文與湘東王令曰：「王筠本自舊手，後進有蕭愷可稱，信為才子。

translations.literal: Jianwen wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong: "Wang Jun was already an old hand; among the rising generation Xiao Kai may be named—he is truly a literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen wrote to the Prince of Xiangdong: "Wang Jun was already a seasoned writer; among the younger men, Xiao Kai deserves mention—he is truly a man of letters.

sentences.zh: 」先是太學博士顧野王奉令撰玉篇，簡文嫌其書詳略未當，以愷博學，于文字尤善，使更與學士刪改。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Erudite Gu Yewang of the Imperial Academy had been ordered to compile the Jade Chapters; Jianwen found the book's detail and omission inappropriate. Because Kai was broadly learned and especially skilled in characters, he was made to revise it further with academy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, Academy Erudite Gu Yewang had been ordered to compile the Jade Chapters; Jianwen found its balance of detail and omission unsatisfactory. Because Kai was broadly learned and especially adept with written forms, he was set to revise it again with academy scholars.

sentences.zh: 太清中，卒於侍中。

translations.literal: During Taqing, he died while serving as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Taqing era while serving as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子顯弟子云。

translations.literal: Zixian's son Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian's son was Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 子雲字景喬，年十二，齊建武四年，封新浦縣侯。

translations.literal: Ziyun, courtesy name Jingqiao, at age twelve in the fourth year of Jianwu of Qi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinpu County.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun, styled Jingqiao, was at twelve enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinpu County in the fourth year of Jianwu under Qi.

sentences.zh: 自製拜章，便有文采。

translations.literal: He composed his own submission of thanks, and it already showed literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted his own memorial of thanks, and it already showed literary grace.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，降爵為子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Tianjian era, his rank was reduced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Liang's Tianjian reign, his title was reduced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 及長，勤學有文藻，弱冠撰晉書，至年二十六，書成百餘卷，表奏之，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied diligently and had literary gifts; at twenty he began compiling a History of Jin, and by age twenty-six the work reached more than a hundred juan; he memorialized it to the throne, and an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he studied hard and wrote well; at twenty he began a History of Jin, and by twenty-six had completed more than a hundred juan, which he submitted to the throne; an edict ordered it stored in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 子雲性沈靜，不樂仕進，風神閑曠，任性不群。

translations.literal: Ziyun's nature was quiet and still; he took no pleasure in advancing in office; his spirit was free and expansive, following his nature apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun was quiet by nature, uninterested in climbing the ladder of office; his bearing was open and unconfined, and he followed his own bent apart from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 夏月對賓客，恒自裸袒。

translations.literal: In summer months when receiving guests, he would always go bare-chested.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he would receive guests bare-chested.

sentences.zh: 而兄弟不睦，乃至吉凶不相吊問，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was not harmonious with his brothers—even at times of fortune or misfortune they did not condole or inquire of one another; public opinion held this against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was estranged from his brothers, so that in joy or sorrow they neither visited nor consoled one another; public opinion faulted him for this.

sentences.zh: 年三十，方起家為秘書郎，遷太子舍人，撰東宮新記奏之，敕賜束帛。

translations.literal: At thirty he first entered service as a Secretary; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household, compiled New Records of the Eastern Palace and submitted it, and an edict granted him silks.
translations.idiomatic: Not until thirty did he first take office, as a Secretary; he was then promoted to Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household, submitted New Records of the Eastern Palace, and received an imperial gift of silks.

sentences.zh: 累遷丹陽郡丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Assistant Administrator of Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Assistant Administrator of Danyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹為丹陽尹，深相賞好，如布衣之交。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, served as Prefect of Danyang, they deeply appreciated each other, like friends in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, served as Prefect of Danyang, they held each other in deep regard, like friends without rank between them.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，為臨川內史，在郡以和理稱，人吏悅之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong, he served as Interior Governor of Linchuan; in the commandery he was known for harmonious governance, and people and officials were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongdatong he became Interior Governor of Linchuan, where he was praised for fair and conciliatory rule; officials and people alike were content.

sentences.zh: 還除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Palace Attendant and Rector of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Palace Attendant and then as Rector of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 梁初，郊廟未革牲牷，樂辭皆沈約撰，至是承用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, the suburban and ancestral rites had not yet changed their sacrificial victims; all the ritual lyrics had been composed by Shen Yue, and up to this time were still in use.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Liang, the suburban and temple sacrifices had not yet revised their offerings, and all the ritual lyrics were Shen Yue's, still in use as before.

sentences.zh: 子雲啟宜改之，敕答曰：「此是主者守株，宜急改也。

translations.literal: Ziyun memorialized that they should be changed; the edict replied: "Those in charge have been clinging to the old stump—they should be changed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun memorialized that they ought to be revised; the reply came: "Those responsible have been waiting like a man guarding a tree stump—they must be changed without delay.

sentences.zh: 」仍使子雲撰定。

translations.literal: " He was still made to have Ziyun compile and set them.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziyun was then ordered to draft the new texts.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「郊廟歌辭，應須典誥大語，不得雜用子史文章淺言。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Suburban and temple hymn texts must use the grand language of canonical edicts; one must not mix in shallow phrasing from the Masters and Histories.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Suburban and temple hymns must employ the solemn language of canonical edicts, and must not borrow shallow turns from the Masters, Histories, and belles lettres.

sentences.zh: 而沈約所撰，亦多舛謬。

translations.literal: Yet what Shen Yue had composed also contained many errors.
translations.idiomatic: Even Shen Yue's versions contained many mistakes.

sentences.zh: 」子雲作成，敕並施用。

translations.literal: " When Ziyun finished, an edict ordered all to be put into use.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ziyun completed the work, an edict ordered all the new texts adopted.

sentences.zh: 子雲善草隸，為時楷法，自雲善效鍾元常、王逸少而微變字體。

translations.literal: Ziyun was skilled in cursive and clerical script, setting the standard of the age; he himself said he was adept at emulating Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi while subtly altering the letter forms.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun excelled in cursive and clerical script and set the standard of his age; he said himself that he followed Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi while subtly reshaping the forms of the characters.

sentences.zh: 嘗答敕云：「臣昔不能拔賞，隨時所貴，規摹子敬，多歷年所。

translations.literal: He once replied to an imperial command: "Your subject formerly could not discern true worth and followed what the age prized; I modeled myself on Zijing for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He once answered an imperial command: "Your subject once lacked the eye to discern excellence and followed whatever the age admired; for many years I took Wang Xianzhi as my model.

sentences.zh: 年二十六著晉史，至二王列傳，欲作論草隸法，言不盡意，遂不能成，略指論飛白一事而已。

translations.literal: At twenty-six I was compiling the History of Jin; when I reached the biographies of the Two Wangs, I wished to compose a treatise on cursive and clerical methods, but words could not fully express the meaning, so I could not complete it—I only briefly touched on the matter of feibai.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six, while compiling my History of Jin, I reached the biographies of the Two Wangs and wished to write on cursive and clerical methods; words could not carry the meaning, so I could not finish—I touched only briefly on feibai.

sentences.zh: 十許年，始見敕旨論書一卷，商略筆狀，洞澈字體，始變子敬，全范元常。

translations.literal: After some ten years, I first saw an imperial command to compose a one-juan treatise on calligraphy; I considered brush techniques and penetrated the essence of letter forms, then began to shift from Zijing and fully modeled Yuan chang.
translations.idiomatic: Some ten years later I received an imperial command to write a one-juan treatise on calligraphy; weighing brushwork and penetrating the forms of characters, I began to turn from Xianzhi and take Zhong Yao as my full model.

sentences.zh: 逮爾以來，自覺功進。

translations.literal: From that time on, I have felt my skill advance.
translations.idiomatic: Since then I have felt my craft steadily improve.

sentences.zh: 」其書跡雅為武帝所重，帝嘗論書曰：「筆力勁駿，心手相應，巧逾杜度，美過崔寔，當與元常並驅爭先。

translations.literal: " His calligraphic traces were greatly valued by Emperor Wu; the Emperor once discussed calligraphy and said: "Brush strength vigorous and swift, heart and hand in accord—skill surpassing Du Du, beauty exceeding Cui Shi—he should race neck and neck with Yuan chang.
translations.idiomatic: " His writing was greatly prized by Emperor Wu, who once remarked on calligraphy: "His brush is forceful and fleet, heart and hand move as one; in skill he surpasses Du Du, in beauty he exceeds Cui Shi—he should run neck and neck with Zhong Yao.

sentences.zh: 」其見賞如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the appreciation shown him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 出為東陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 百濟國使人至建鄴求書，逢子雲為郡，維舟將發。

translations.literal: An envoy from Baekje came to Jiankang seeking calligraphy; he happened upon Ziyun while the latter was in the commandery, with his boat moored and about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy from Baekje came to Jiankang seeking calligraphy and found Ziyun serving in the prefecture, his boat moored and ready to sail.

sentences.zh: 使人於渚次候之，望船三十許步，行拜行前。

translations.literal: The envoy waited for him at the shore; sighting the boat from some thirty paces, he walked forward performing bows.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy waited on the bank; when he saw the boat from some thirty paces off, he walked forward bowing as he came.

sentences.zh: 子雲遣問之，答曰：「侍中尺牘之美，遠流海外，今日所求，唯在名跡。

translations.literal: Ziyun sent someone to inquire; the reply came: "The beauty of the Palace Attendant's letters has flowed far overseas; what I seek today is only your celebrated traces.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun sent someone to ask his business; the envoy answered: "The Palace Attendant's letters are famed even overseas; what I seek today is only your signature and hand.

sentences.zh: 」子雲乃為停船三日，書三十紙與之，獲金貨數百萬。

translations.literal: " Ziyun then halted his boat for three days, wrote thirty sheets for him, and received several million in gold and goods.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziyun thereupon moored for three days, wrote thirty sheets for the envoy, and was paid several million in gold and goods.

sentences.zh: 性吝，自外答餉不書好紙，好事者重加賂遺，以要其答。

translations.literal: His nature was stingy; when replying to gifts from outside he would not write on fine paper; enthusiasts would lavish extra bribes to obtain his reply.
translations.idiomatic: He was miserly by nature: when answering gifts from outsiders he would not use good paper, so collectors would pile on further presents to secure a reply.

sentences.zh: 子特字世達，早知名，亦善草隸，時人比之衛恒、衛瓘。

translations.literal: Zite, courtesy name Shida, was known early; he too was skilled in cursive and clerical script, and people of the time compared him to Wei Heng and Wei Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Zite, styled Shida, won early fame; he too excelled in cursive and clerical script, and contemporaries likened him to Wei Heng and Wei Guan.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗使特書，及奏，帝曰：「子敬之跡不及逸少，蕭特之書遂逼于父。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once had Te write; when it was presented, the Emperor said: "Zijing's traces cannot match Yishao; Xiao Te's writing nearly presses his father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once had Zite write; when the work was presented, the Emperor said: "Xianzhi's hand cannot equal Xizhi's, yet Xiao Te's writing nearly matches his father's.

sentences.zh: 」位太子舍人，海鹽令，坐事免。

translations.literal: " He held the posts of Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household and Magistrate of Haiyan, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: " He served as Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household and as Magistrate of Haiyan, and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 先子雲卒，遺啟簡文求為墓誌銘，帝為制銘焉。

translations.literal: He died before Ziyun; in a final memorial he asked Jianwen for an epitaph, and the Emperor composed one.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Ziyun; in a final memorial he asked Jianwen to compose his epitaph, and the Emperor wrote it.

sentences.zh: 子雲弟子暉字景光，少涉學，亦有文才。

translations.literal: Ziyun's son Zihui, courtesy name Jingguang, studied widely in youth and also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun's son Zihui, styled Jingguang, read broadly in youth and showed literary talent as well.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜，寡嗜欲，嘗預重雲殿聽制講三慧經，退為講賦奏之，甚見賞。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil and still, with few desires; he once attended at Chongyun Hall to hear the Emperor's lecture on the Sutra of the Three Wisdoms, and upon withdrawing composed a rhapsody on the lecture and submitted it; it was greatly appreciated.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and sparing in his appetites, he once attended the Emperor's exposition of the Sutra of the Three Wisdoms at Chongyun Hall; afterward he wrote a rhapsody on the lecture and submitted it, and it was much admired.

sentences.zh: 卒于驃騎長史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Chief Clerk to the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Chief Clerk to the Rapid Cavalry General.
